```text
> Sub-issue of #23 · **P1** · estimate **5 points** (medium) · blocked by #56

## User Story
As a user who suspects Gitea has keyboard shortcuts but cannot find them, I want to press `?` on
any page and see every available shortcut grouped by area, so that I can learn them without
reading the source or the docs.

## User Scenario
A user is looking at an issue. They press `?`. A dialog opens in the centre of the page titled
"Keyboard shortcuts", listing the shortcuts under headings such as "Site-wide" and "Repository",
each row showing the keys as `<kbd>` elements next to a description. Focus moves into the dialog;
Tab cycles inside it and does not reach the page behind. They press Escape, the dialog closes, and
focus returns to where it was.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given any page with focus on the document body, when the user presses `?`, then a
      dialog opens listing one row per shortcut registered in #56, with the keys and the
      description.
- [ ] AC2: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses Escape, then it closes and focus
      returns to the element that was focused before it opened.
- [ ] AC3: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses Tab repeatedly, then focus stays inside
      the dialog and never lands on a control on the page behind it.
- [ ] AC4: Given focus is in a comment textarea, when the user types `?`, then a literal `?` is
      inserted and the dialog does not open.
- [ ] AC5: Given a new shortcut is registered with a description and a category, when the dialog
      is opened, then it appears under that category with no change to the dialog's own code.
- [ ] AC6: Given the page is served in a non-English locale, when the dialog is opened, then the
      title and section headings are rendered from locale keys, not hard-coded English.
- [ ] AC7: A Playwright test in `tests/e2e/` covers AC1, AC2 and AC4 and passes `assertNoJsError`.

## Out of Scope
- Adding shortcuts. The dialog lists whatever #56's registry holds, which at merge time is `s`,
  `t` and `?` itself.
- Editing or remapping a shortcut from the dialog.
- The opt-out checkbox — that is #60.
- A printable or documentation-page version of the list.

## Open Questions
- Should the dialog also be reachable by mouse, from a footer link? Proposed: not in this issue,
  to keep it to one entry point that the e2e test can cover.

## Design Decision
**Decision:** Build the dialog on the native `<dialog>` element with `showModal()`, not on
Fomantic's modal.

**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Fomantic modal via `showFomanticModal` in
`web_src/js/modules/fomantic/modal.ts`, which is what the rest of the codebase uses today.
(b) A plain `<div>` with a hand-written focus trap and backdrop.

**Rationale:** `.claude-students/docs/frontend-js.md` says Fomantic is deprecated and new features
must not be built on it — and given this issue's sibling #25 exists to remove Fomantic for
accessibility reasons, adding a new Fomantic modal to the accessibility feature would be
self-defeating. `showModal()` gives the focus trap (AC3), Escape-to-close (AC2), focus restoration
and `aria-modal` semantics from the browser, so (b) would mean hand-writing behaviour the platform
already gets right, which is exactly the class of bug #25 is about.

**Consequences:** Easier — AC2 and AC3 are largely satisfied by the browser, and the dialog has no
jQuery dependency. Harder — `<dialog>` styling differs from every other modal in Gitea, so the
dialog needs its own CSS and will not automatically match the Fomantic modals around it; the
`::backdrop` pseudo-element in particular needs theming against both light and dark themes.

## Scope
medium (5 points)
```

```text
> Sub-issue of #23 · **P3 — Sprint 2 carryover** · estimate **2 points** (small) · blocked by #56, #57

## User Story
As a user of speech recognition software, I want to turn off Gitea's single-character shortcuts,
so that dictating a word into the page does not fire a shortcut and navigate me away from what I
was writing.

## User Scenario
Someone using voice control finds that saying a word while the page has focus keeps triggering the
file finder. They press `?`, see a checkbox at the bottom of the shortcut dialog reading "Enable
character key shortcuts", and clear it. The shortcut list greys out. They close the dialog, dictate
freely, and the setting is still off the next time they open Gitea in that browser.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given the shortcut help dialog, when the user clears the "Enable character key
      shortcuts" checkbox, then pressing `s`, `t` or any `g` sequence has no effect.
- [ ] AC2: Given shortcuts are disabled, when the user reloads the page, then they are still
      disabled.
- [ ] AC3: Given shortcuts are disabled, when the user presses `?`, then the help dialog still
      opens, so the setting can be turned back on without a mouse.
- [ ] AC4: Given shortcuts are disabled, when the user re-checks the box, then `s` focuses the
      repo sidebar search again without a reload.
- [ ] AC5: Given a browser with storage blocked, when the page loads, then shortcuts default to
      enabled and no error is thrown.
- [ ] AC6: Unit tests in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` cover AC1, AC3 and AC5.

## Out of Scope
- Remapping individual shortcuts, or turning off one shortcut at a time.
- Storing the preference on the server or syncing it across devices or browsers.
- A copy of the toggle in the user settings pages.

## Open Questions
- WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.4 is satisfied by "turn off", "remap" or "active on focus only". This issue
  takes "turn off" as the cheapest complete option; confirm that is the team's reading.

## Design Decision
**Decision:** Store the preference in `localStorage` and keep `?` itself exempt from the toggle.

**Alternatives Considered:** (a) A server-side user setting, as a column on the user table with a
checkbox on the appearance settings page. (b) Storing it in `localStorage` but suppressing every
shortcut including `?`.

**Rationale:** (a) needs a migration and a settings form for a preference that is per-browser by
nature — someone using voice control on one machine does not need it off everywhere — and a
migration is more than this issue is worth. (b) is more literally correct against SC 2.1.4, but it
leaves a keyboard-only user who has disabled shortcuts with no keyboard route back to the dialog,
which trades one accessibility failure for another; keeping exactly one exempt key is the standard
escape hatch.

**Consequences:** Easier — no server change, no migration, and the flag is a single module-level
read the registry consults before dispatching. Harder — the preference does not follow the user to
another browser or machine and is invisible to support; and `?` staying live is a documented
deliberate exception that needs a comment in the code so nobody "fixes" it later.

## Scope
small (2 points)
```

```text
function extractSelectedMarkdown(container: HTMLElement) {
  const selection = window.getSelection();
  if (!selection?.rangeCount) return '';
  const range = selection.getRangeAt(0);
  if (!container.contains(range.commonAncestorContainer)) return '';

  // todo: if commonAncestorContainer parent has "[data-markdown-original-content]" attribute, use the parent's markdown content
  // otherwise, use the selected HTML content and respect all "[data-markdown-original-content]/[data-markdown-generated-content]" attributes
  const contents = selection.getRangeAt(0).cloneContents();
  const el = document.createElement('div');
  el.append(contents);
  return convertHtmlToMarkdown(el);
}

async function tryOnQuoteReply(e: Event) {
  const clickTarget = (e.target as HTMLElement).closest('.quote-reply');
  if (!clickTarget) return;

  e.preventDefault();
  const contentToQuoteId = clickTarget.getAttribute('data-target');
  const targetRawToQuote = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`#${contentToQuoteId}.raw-content`)!;
  const targetMarkupToQuote = targetRawToQuote.parentElement!.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.render-content.markup')!;
  let contentToQuote = extractSelectedMarkdown(targetMarkupToQuote);
  if (!contentToQuote) contentToQuote = targetRawToQuote.textContent;
  const quotedContent = `${contentToQuote.replace(/^/mg, '> ')}\n\n`;

  let editor;
  if (clickTarget.classList.contains('quote-reply-diff')) {
    const replyBtn = clickTarget.closest('.comment-code-cloud')!.querySelector<HTMLElement>('button.comment-form-reply')!;
    editor = await handleReply(replyBtn);
  } else {
    // for normal issue/comment page
    editor = getComboMarkdownEditor(document.querySelector('#comment-form .combo-markdown-editor'))!;
  }

  if (editor.value()) {
    editor.value(`${editor.value()}\n\n${quotedContent}`);
  } else {
    editor.value(quotedContent);
  }
  editor.focus();
  editor.moveCursorToEnd();
}

export function initRepoIssueCommentEdit() {
  document.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    tryOnEditContent(e); // Edit issue or comment content
    tryOnQuoteReply(e); // Quote reply to the comment editor
  });
}
```

```text
  isUploading() {

  setupTab() {
    const elTabular = this.container.querySelector('.ui.tabular');
    if (!elTabular) return;
    this.tabEditor = this.container.querySelector('[data-tab-for="markdown-writer"]')!;
    this.tabPreviewer = this.container.querySelector('[data-tab-for="markdown-previewer"]')!;
    const panelEditor = this.container.querySelector('.ui.tab[data-tab-panel="markdown-writer"]')!;
    const panelPreviewer = this.container.querySelector('.ui.tab[data-tab-panel="markdown-previewer"]')!;

    // Fomantic Tab requires the "data-tab" to be globally unique.
    // So here it uses our defined "data-tab-for" and "data-tab-panel" to generate the "data-tab" attribute for Fomantic.
    const tabIdSuffix = generateElemId();
    this.tabEditor.setAttribute('data-tab', `markdown-writer-${tabIdSuffix}`);
    this.tabPreviewer.setAttribute('data-tab', `markdown-previewer-${tabIdSuffix}`);
    panelEditor.setAttribute('data-tab', `markdown-writer-${tabIdSuffix}`);
    panelPreviewer.setAttribute('data-tab', `markdown-previewer-${tabIdSuffix}`);
    initTabSwitcher(elTabular);

    this.tabEditor.addEventListener('click', () => {
      requestAnimationFrame(() => {
        this.focus();
      });
    });

    this.tabPreviewer.addEventListener('click', async () => {
      const formData = new FormData();
      formData.append('mode', this.previewMode);
      formData.append('context', this.previewContext);
      formData.append('text', this.value());
      const response = await POST(this.previewUrl, {data: formData});
      const data = await response.text();
      addTablePanelTippy.hide();
    });
  }

  switchTabToEditor() {
    this.tabEditor!.click(); // when this function is called, the tab must exist
  }

  prepareEasyMDEToolbarActions() {
    hideElem(this.textareaMarkdownToolbar);
  }

  value(v?: any) {
    if (v === undefined) {
      if (this.easyMDE) {
        return this.easyMDE.value();
      }
      return this.textarea.value;
    }

    if (this.easyMDE) {
      this.easyMDE.value(v);
    } else {
      this.textarea.value = v;
    }
    this.textareaAutosize?.resizeToFit();
  }

  focus() {
    if (this.easyMDE) {
      this.easyMDE.codemirror.focus();
    } else {
      this.textarea.focus();
    }
  }

  moveCursorToEnd() {
    this.textarea.focus();
    this.textarea.setSelectionRange(this.textarea.value.length, this.textarea.value.length);
    if (this.easyMDE) {
      this.easyMDE.codemirror.focus();
      this.easyMDE.codemirror.setCursor(this.easyMDE.codemirror.lineCount(), 0);
    }
  }

  get userPreferredEditor(): string {
    return localUserSettings.getString(`markdown-editor-${this.previewMode ?? 'default'}`);
  }
```

```text
import {registerGlobalInitFunc} from './observer.ts';
import {hideElem, toggleElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';

const sequenceTimeoutMs = 1500; // the longest wait between the keys of a sequence

export type Shortcut = {
  keys: string, // keys pressed one after another, separated by spaces, e.g. "g c"
  description: string, // translated
  section?: string, // translated
  element?: HTMLElement, // the shortcut only exists while this element is in the document
  action: () => void,
};

export type ShortcutInfo = Pick<Shortcut, 'keys' | 'description' | 'section'>;

function isActive(shortcut: Shortcut): boolean {
  return !shortcut.element || shortcut.element.isConnected;
}

// returns the shortcut for exactly these keys, 'prefix' if they start a longer sequence, or null
function matchKeys(shortcuts: Shortcut[], keys: string): Shortcut | 'prefix' | null {
  for (const shortcut of shortcuts) {
    if (shortcut.keys === keys) return shortcut;
    if (shortcut.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `)) return 'prefix';
  }
  return null;
}

export class ShortcutRegistry {
  shortcuts: Shortcut[] = [];
  pendingKeys = ''; // the start of a sequence pressed so far
  pendingTime = 0;

  register(shortcut: Shortcut) {
    const keys = shortcut.keys.toLowerCase();
    // a shortcut whose element has left the page, e.g. a hint replaced by file tree navigation, gives way to the new one
    this.shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    const conflict = this.shortcuts.find((s) => s.keys === keys || s.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `) || keys.startsWith(`${s.keys} `));
    if (conflict) throw new Error(`Keyboard shortcut "${keys}" conflicts with "${conflict.keys}"`);
    this.shortcuts.push({...shortcut, keys});
  }

  list(): ShortcutInfo[] {
    return this.shortcuts.filter(isActive).map(({keys, description, section}) => ({keys, description, section}));
  }

  handleKeyDown(e: KeyboardEvent) {
    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;
    // the key was already used by a widget such as a menu, or is being typed into a field
    if (e.defaultPrevented || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey || target.matches('input, textarea, select') || target.isContentEditable) {
      this.pendingKeys = '';
      return;
    }
    if (e.key === 'Shift') return; // not a press of its own, e.g. on the way to "?"
    if (e.repeat) return; // a held key runs its shortcut once, and doesn't start over after a sequence

    if (Date.now() - this.pendingTime > sequenceTimeoutMs) this.pendingKeys = '';
    const key = e.key.toLowerCase();
    const shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    let keys = this.pendingKeys ? `${this.pendingKeys} ${key}` : key;
    let match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    if (!match && keys !== key) {
      // the key does not continue the sequence, so it acts as a fresh press
      keys = key;
      match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    }
    this.pendingKeys = '';
    if (!match) return;

    e.preventDefault();
    if (match === 'prefix') {
      this.pendingKeys = keys;
      this.pendingTime = Date.now();
    } else {
      match.action();
    }
  }
}

const globalRegistry = new ShortcutRegistry();

// Adds a keyboard shortcut to the page. Throws if the keys clash with an existing shortcut.
export function registerShortcut(shortcut: Shortcut) {
  globalRegistry.register(shortcut);
}

// The shortcuts available on the current page, e.g. for a help dialog
export function getShortcuts(): ShortcutInfo[] {
  return globalRegistry.list();
}

export function initShortcutKbd(kbd: HTMLElement) {
  // Handle initial state: hide the kbd hint if the associated input already has a value
  // (e.g., from browser autofill or back/forward navigation cache)
  const elem = elemFromKbd(kbd)!;
  if (elem.value) hideElem(kbd);
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
  kbd.setAttribute('aria-keyshortcuts', kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!);

    keys: kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-keys')!,
    description: elem.placeholder,
    section: kbd.getAttribute('data-shortcut-section') ?? undefined,
    element: kbd,
    action: () => elem.focus(),
  });
}

function shortcutWrapper(el: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  const parent = el.parentElement;
  return parent?.matches('.global-shortcut-wrapper') ? parent : null;
}

function elemFromKbd(kbd: HTMLElement): HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(kbd)?.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input, textarea') || null;
}

function kbdFromElem(input: HTMLElement): HTMLElement | null {
  return shortcutWrapper(input)?.querySelector<HTMLElement>('kbd') || null;
}
```

```text
export function showFomanticModal(el: Element | null, opts: ModalOpts = {}) {

}

  $(el).modal('hide');
}
```

```text
    if (restoreFocus && focusInPopup) this.trigger.focus();
  }

  onPointerDownOutside = (e: Event) => {
    if (!this.contains(e.target as Node)) this.close(false);
  };

  // a native button fires "click" on Space keyup, which would toggle the menu shut again or double-activate an item
  preventSpaceClick = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.key === ' ') e.preventDefault();
  };

  onTriggerKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.isComposing) return;
    if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ' || e.key === 'ArrowDown') {
      this.open('first');
    } else if (e.key === 'ArrowUp') {
      this.open('last');
    } else {
      return;
    }
    e.preventDefault();
  };

  onPopupKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.isComposing) return;
    const items = this.items();
    const current = items.indexOf(e.target as HTMLElement);
    if (e.key === 'Tab') {
      // focus the trigger and let the default action move on from there
      this.close(true);
      return;
    }
    if (e.key === 'Escape') {
      e.stopPropagation(); // don't also close a surrounding modal
      this.close(true);
    } else if (e.key === 'ArrowDown') {
      items[(current + 1) % items.length].focus();
    } else if (e.key === 'ArrowUp') {
      items.at(current <= 0 ? -1 : current - 1)!.focus();
    } else if (e.key === 'Home') {
      items[0].focus();
    } else if (e.key === 'End') {
      items.at(-1)!.focus();
    } else if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') {
      if (current < 0) return;
      items[current].click();
    } else if (e.key.length === 1 && !e.ctrlKey && !e.metaKey && !e.altKey) {
      this.focusByFirstChar(items, current, e.key);
    } else {
      return;
    }
    e.preventDefault();
  };

  focusByFirstChar(items: HTMLElement[], current: number, char: string) {
    const lower = char.toLowerCase();
    for (let i = 1; i <= items.length; i++) {
      const item = items[(current + i) % items.length];
      if (item.textContent.trim().toLowerCase().startsWith(lower)) {
        item.focus();
        return;
      }
    }
  }
});
```

```text
test('profile menu is operable by keyboard', async ({page}) => {
  await login(page);
  await page.goto('/');
  const trigger = page.getByRole('button', {name: 'Profile and Settings…'});
  const menu = page.getByRole('menu', {name: 'Profile and Settings…'});

  await trigger.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(trigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Profile', exact: true})).toBeFocused();

  const menuBox = (await menu.boundingBox())!;
  expect(menuBox.x + menuBox.width).toBeLessThanOrEqual(page.viewportSize()!.width);

  await page.keyboard.press('End');
  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Sign Out'})).toBeFocused();
  await page.keyboard.press('Home');
  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Profile', exact: true})).toBeFocused();
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await expect(menu).toBeHidden();
  await expect(trigger).toBeFocused();

  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  for (const name of ['Starred', 'Subscriptions', 'Settings']) {
    await page.keyboard.press('s');
    await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name})).toBeFocused();
  }
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/user\/settings$/);
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});
```

```text
  if (status !== 302 && status !== 303) throw new Error(`login as ${username} failed: HTTP ${status}`);
```

```markdown
> Sub-issue of #23 · **P1** · estimate **5 points** (medium) · blocked by #56

## User Story
As a keyboard user who suspects Gitea has shortcuts but cannot find them, I want to press `?` on any page and see the shortcuts that work on that page, grouped by section, so that I can learn them without reading the source or the docs.

## User Scenario
A user is on a repository's home page. They press `?`. A dialog titled "Keyboard shortcuts" opens in the middle of the page. It lists `?` under "General" and `S` ("Search code…") under "Repository", each row showing the keys as `<kbd>` elements next to the description. Focus moves into the dialog, and Tab cycles inside it without reaching the page behind. They press Escape. The dialog closes and focus returns to where it was.

On their notifications page, which has no page-specific shortcuts, `?` opens the same dialog listing only `?`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given any page that loads Gitea's main script, with focus outside a text field, when the user presses `?`, then a dialog titled "Keyboard shortcuts" opens with one row for each shortcut in #56's registry on that page (`getShortcuts()`), showing its keys and description.
- [ ] AC2: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses Escape, then it closes and focus returns to the element that was focused before it opened.
- [ ] AC3: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses Tab repeatedly, then focus stays inside the dialog and never reaches a control on the page behind it.
- [ ] AC4: Given focus is in an input, textarea or editable area, when the user types `?`, then a literal `?` is typed and the dialog does not open.
- [ ] AC5: Given shortcuts with different section labels, when the dialog opens, then each section is a heading with its shortcuts under it. A shortcut registered later with a new section appears under that section with no change to the dialog's code.
- [ ] AC6: Given the page is served in a non-English locale, when the dialog opens, then its title, its close button's accessible name and the "General" section come from locale keys, not hard-coded English.
- [ ] AC7: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses `?` again or clicks outside it, then nothing else opens and the dialog stays as it is (`?` does not stack a second dialog).
- [ ] AC8: A Playwright test in `tests/e2e/` covers AC1, AC2 and AC4 on a repository home page and calls `assertNoJsError`; unit tests in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` cover the grouping in AC5.

## Out of Scope
- Adding shortcuts other than `?` itself. The `g` shortcuts are #58, `c` is #59 and `r` is #95; each appears in the dialog once it is registered.
- Listing shortcuts that belong to other pages. The dialog shows what works on the current page.
- Editing or remapping a shortcut from the dialog.
- The setting to turn shortcuts off. That is #60, which adds a checkbox to this dialog.
- A link to the dialog in the footer or a menu, and a printable or documentation page of shortcuts.

## Open Questions
- Should the dialog also be reachable by mouse, for example from a footer link? Proposed: not in this issue, so there is one entry point and the e2e test covers it.
- Should a click on the backdrop close the dialog? AC7 proposes no, to match Escape as the single way out besides the close button. Reviewer to confirm.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: the dialog element
**Decision:** Build the dialog on the native `<dialog>` element, opened with `showModal()`.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) A Fomantic modal shown with `showFomanticModal` from `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/modal.ts`, which is what Gitea's other modals use today.
- (b) A plain `<div>` with a hand-written focus trap, backdrop and Escape handler.

**Rationale:** `.claude-students/docs/frontend-js.md` says Fomantic is deprecated and new features must not be built on it. Sibling issue #25 exists to remove Fomantic from the accessibility path, so a new Fomantic modal on an accessibility feature works against it. `showModal()` gives the browser's own focus trap (AC3), Escape to close (AC2), focus return and `aria-modal` semantics, so (b) would mean rewriting behaviour the browser already has, which is the kind of bug #25 is about.

**Consequences:** AC2 and AC3 come mostly from the browser, and the dialog has no jQuery dependency. It is the first native `<dialog>` in Gitea, so there is no shared helper to reuse and its look has to be styled to match `web_src/css/modules/modal.css` by hand.

### Decision 2: where the dialog's markup and text come from
**Decision:** Render the empty `<dialog>` once in the base page template (next to the footer script) with its translated title, close label and "General" heading as server-rendered text, hidden until opened. JavaScript fills in the rows from `getShortcuts()` when `?` is pressed.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Build the whole dialog in JavaScript, and add its strings to `window.config.i18n` in `templates/base/head_script.tmpl`.
- (b) A Vue component mounted on demand, with its strings passed as `data-locale-*` attributes.

**Rationale:** `templates/base/head_script.tmpl` says page-specific text should not go into `window.config.i18n`, which every page downloads. The #56 registry already takes its descriptions and section labels as server-translated text, so a server-rendered shell follows the same pattern and needs no new i18n plumbing. Vue (b) adds a component and a mount for a static list, which `.claude-students/docs/frontend-vue-components.md` advises against for markup this simple.

**Consequences:** Every page carries a few hundred bytes of hidden markup. The `?` shortcut needs its own `<kbd>`-less registration in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts` (or the new dialog module) with the server-rendered "General" label and description read from the dialog's data attributes.

## Scope
medium (5 points)
```

```markdown
> Sub-issue of #23 · **P2** · estimate **2 points** (small) · blocked by #56, #57

## User Story
As a user of speech recognition software, I want to turn off Gitea's single-character shortcuts, so that dictating a word while the page has focus does not fire a shortcut and move me away from what I was doing.

## User Scenario
Someone using voice control finds that saying a word on a repository page keeps jumping focus into the code search box. They press `?`, see a checkbox at the bottom of the shortcut dialog reading "Enable character key shortcuts", and clear it. The listed shortcuts grey out. They close the dialog and dictate freely. The next time they open Gitea in that browser, shortcuts are still off.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given the shortcut dialog from #57, when the user clears the "Enable character key shortcuts" checkbox, then pressing any registered shortcut other than `?` (for example `s` on a repository home page) does nothing, and the key reaches the page as if no shortcut existed.
- [ ] AC2: Given shortcuts are turned off, when the user reloads the page or opens another page in the same browser, then they are still off.
- [ ] AC3: Given shortcuts are turned off, when the user presses `?`, then the dialog still opens, so the setting can be turned back on without a mouse.
- [ ] AC4: Given shortcuts are turned off, when the user checks the box again, then `s` on a repository home page focuses the code search box again without a reload.
- [ ] AC5: Given a browser where storage access throws, when a page loads, then shortcuts are on, the checkbox is checked and no uncaught error occurs.
- [ ] AC6: Given shortcuts are turned off, when the user presses `g` and then another key, then no half-finished sequence is kept and neither key runs a shortcut.
- [ ] AC7: Given the page is served in a non-English locale, when the dialog opens, then the checkbox label comes from a locale key.
- [ ] AC8: Unit tests in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` cover AC1, AC3, AC5 and AC6; the e2e test from #57 is extended to cover AC2.

## Out of Scope
- Remapping shortcuts, or turning off one shortcut at a time.
- Storing the setting on the server or syncing it across browsers.
- A copy of the setting on the user settings pages.
- Keys owned by widgets, such as the code editor and the menus' type-to-jump; #56 already leaves those alone.

## Open Questions
- WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.4 accepts "turn off", "remap" or "active only on focus". This issue picks "turn off" as the smallest complete option. Reviewer to confirm that reading.

## Design Decision
**Decision:** Store the setting in the browser with the existing `localUserSettings` wrapper (`web_src/js/modules/user-settings.ts`), under the key `keyboard-shortcuts-enabled` with a default of `true`. The registry's single dispatch point (`handleKeyDown` in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts`) checks it before running any shortcut except `?`.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) A server-side user setting: a column on the user table and a checkbox on the Appearance settings page.
- (b) The same browser setting, but turning off every shortcut including `?`.

**Rationale:** (a) needs a migration and a settings form for a preference that belongs to one browser. Someone who uses voice control on one machine does not need shortcuts off everywhere, and a migration costs more than this issue is worth. (b) follows SC 2.1.4 more literally, but a keyboard-only user who turned shortcuts off would have no keyboard way back to the checkbox. That swaps one accessibility failure for another. Keeping exactly one exempt key is the usual way out. `localUserSettings` already wraps every storage call in try/catch, so AC5 needs no new error handling.

**Consequences:** No server change and no migration. The setting does not follow the user to another browser and support cannot see it. `?` staying live is a deliberate exception, so the check carries a short comment saying why, to stop someone "fixing" it later.

## Scope
small (2 points)
```

```markdown
> Sub-issue of #23 · estimate **2 points** (small) · blocked by #56; listed in the dialog once #57 lands

## User Story
As a user replying on an issue or pull request, I want GitHub's `r` shortcut to quote the text I have selected into my reply, or take me straight to the reply box when nothing is selected, so that I can answer a specific point without scrolling to the bottom or opening the comment's menu.

## User Scenario
A maintainer is reading a long issue thread. They select a sentence in someone's comment and press `r`. The page scrolls to the reply box at the bottom, the sentence is already in it as a Markdown quote, and the cursor sits after it, ready to type. Later, back at the top of the thread with nothing selected, they press `r` again and land in the same reply box with their text still there.

On a page with no reply box, such as an archived repository or when signed out, `r` does nothing.

| When the user presses `r` with | `r` does |
| --- | --- |
| Text selected inside one comment or the description | Quotes it into the reply box and puts the cursor after it |
| Nothing selected, or a selection that is not inside a single comment | Jumps to the reply box |
| No reply box on the page | Nothing |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given text is selected inside one comment or the issue description on an issue or pull request page, when the user presses `r`, then the text is added to the reply box as a Markdown quote (each line starting with `> `), the box scrolls into view, and the cursor is placed after the quote.
- [ ] AC2: Given the reply box already has text in it, when the user quotes with `r`, then the existing text is kept and the quote is added after it, separated by a blank line.
- [ ] AC3: Given nothing is selected, or the selection spans more than one comment or lies outside any comment, when the user presses `r`, then the reply box scrolls into view with the cursor at the end of its text, and the text is unchanged.
- [ ] AC4: Given the reply box is showing its Preview tab, when the user presses `r`, then it switches back to Write so the cursor and any quote can be seen.
- [ ] AC5: Given a page with no reply box (an archived repository, a signed-out visitor, or a locked conversation the user cannot comment on), when the user presses `r`, then nothing happens and no error is shown.
- [ ] AC6: Given focus is in the reply box or any other text field, when the user types `r`, then a literal `r` is typed.
- [ ] AC7: Given a page where `r` works, when the shortcuts are listed (`getShortcuts()`, shown by #57's dialog), then `r` has the translated "Quote reply" description and a translated section label for issue and pull request pages.
- [ ] AC8: Unit tests cover the selection check in AC1 and AC3; a Playwright test in `tests/e2e/` covers AC1 and AC5 and calls `assertNoJsError`.

## Out of Scope
- Comments in code-review threads and their own reply boxes.
- GitHub's other issue page shortcuts (`a`, `l`, `m`, `q` and `x`).
- GitHub's `c` shortcuts: #59.
- Escape to leave the reply box; Tab already leaves it.
- Submitting the comment. `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+Enter already does that and is not touched here.
- Changes to what the "Quote reply" item in each comment's menu does.
- Showing the shortcuts to the user: #57.

## Open Questions
- None.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: how `r` puts the quote into the reply box
**Decision:** Pull the shared part of the existing "Quote reply" handler (`tryOnQuoteReply` in `web_src/js/features/repo-issue-edit.ts`) into a helper that takes a comment's content element and the reply editor, and appends the quoted selection, focuses the editor and moves the cursor to the end. The menu item and `r` both call it.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Have `r` find the comment the selection is in and click that comment's "Quote reply" menu item from code.
- (b) Write a separate handler for `r` that copies the selection-to-Markdown and append logic.

**Rationale:** (a) needs no refactor, but it depends on the menu markup staying the same, and with nothing selected the menu item quotes the whole comment, which is the opposite of AC3. (b) leaves two copies of the same quoting rules, so a fix to one (for example the lossy HTML-to-Markdown conversion noted in that file) would miss the other. A shared helper keeps one quoting rule, and the menu item keeps its current behaviour.

**Consequences:** The change touches the existing quote-reply code, so its behaviour needs checking by hand or by test as part of this issue. The helper also gains the switch back to the Write tab (AC4), which the menu item lacks today, so the menu item gets that fix too.

### Decision 2: when `r` is registered
**Decision:** Register `r` only when the page has a reply editor (`#comment-form .combo-markdown-editor`), passing that editor as the shortcut's `element` in #56's `registerShortcut`.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Register `r` on every issue and pull request page, and have its action return early when there is no reply box.
- (b) Register it from a `<kbd>` hint in the template, the way #56 registers `s` and `t`.

**Rationale:** The server already decides whether to render the reply form (signed in, not archived, allowed to comment on a locked conversation), so registering from its presence gives AC5 with no permission logic in JavaScript. (a) would list `r` in #57's dialog on pages where it does nothing. (b) adds a visible hint to the reply box that GitHub does not show and the design does not call for.

**Consequences:** `r` and its dialog row exist only where they work. If the reply form is ever rendered on a page where the user cannot actually post, `r` follows the form, not the permission.

## Scope
```

```markdown
> Sub-issue of #25 · **P1** · estimate **2 points** (small) · blocked by nothing

## User Story
As a contributor changing dropdown code, I want an end-to-end test that fails when keyboard operation or the ARIA attributes of a dropdown break, so that the accessibility work from Sprint 1 is not quietly undone by a later refactor.

## User Scenario
A contributor opens a PR that changes `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts`. CI runs the new tests. One opens the template search box on the new-repository page from the keyboard, checks that `aria-expanded` flips to `true`, arrows down, checks that `aria-activedescendant` points at an option in that list, presses Escape and checks the list closed. Their change had dropped `aria-controls`, so the test fails and names that assertion.

A second contributor changes `<aria-menu>` and drops `aria-haspopup` from the navbar avatar menu. The extended navbar test fails and names it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given a signed-in user on `/repo/create`, when a Playwright test moves focus to the repository template search dropdown and opens it from the keyboard, then the test asserts `aria-expanded` is `false` before opening and `true` after.
- [ ] AC2: Given that dropdown is open, when the test presses ArrowDown, then it asserts `aria-activedescendant` names an element that exists and is an option of that dropdown.
- [ ] AC3: Given that dropdown, then the test asserts the input has role `combobox` and that `aria-controls` names the dropdown's list.
- [ ] AC4: Given that dropdown is open, when the test presses Escape, then it asserts the list is hidden and focus is still on the dropdown's input.
- [ ] AC5: Given the signed-in navbar, then `tests/e2e/menus.test.ts` asserts that each `<aria-menu>` trigger has `aria-haspopup="menu"` and that its `aria-controls` names an element with role `menu`.
- [ ] AC6: Each new test calls `assertNoJsError` from `tests/e2e/utils.ts` and finishes in under 2 seconds locally.
- [ ] AC7: The tests pass with `GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='<the test file>' make test-e2e` on `main` as it stands, so they guard current behaviour rather than describe wished-for behaviour.

## Out of Scope
- Fixing anything the tests find. If a dropdown fails an assertion today, file an issue, assert the current behaviour and link the issue in a TODO, rather than changing product code here.
- Keyboard behaviour of the navbar menus already covered by `tests/e2e/menus.test.ts` and `tests/e2e/aria-menu.test.ts` (open, arrow, Home/End, Escape, type to jump).
- Adding `axe-core` or any other accessibility-testing dependency.
- Covering every Fomantic dropdown. One combobox is the target.
- Screen reader output, which no automated test can check.

## Open Questions
- None. (The earlier question about using the new-repository page is now answered by AC1 to AC4.)

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: how to check accessibility
**Decision:** Assert the ARIA attributes and focus position directly with Playwright.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Add `@axe-core/playwright` and assert the page has no violations.
- (b) Write the checks as vitest unit tests against a JSDOM page, next to the existing `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.test.ts`.

**Rationale:** (a) adds a dependency and reports on the page's markup in general rather than on the behaviour Sprint 1 fixed. An axe pass would not have caught the VoiceOver arrow-key bug, and an axe failure elsewhere on the page would fail the test for unrelated reasons. (b) works for `<aria-menu>`, which already has `web_src/js/webcomponents/aria-menu.test.ts`, but not for the combobox. Fomantic's behaviour depends on jQuery, animation classes and real focus, which JSDOM does not reproduce.

**Consequences:** A failing assertion names the exact attribute that broke. The combobox assertions depend on today's Fomantic markup, so a future migration of that dropdown off Fomantic (under #25) will need this test updated. The test carries a comment saying so.

### Decision 2: which dropdowns to test
**Decision:** Test one Fomantic combobox (the template search on `/repo/create`) in a new test file, and add only the missing `aria-haspopup` and `aria-controls` checks to the existing navbar test.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Write the full keyboard suite against the navbar avatar menu, as the first draft of this issue planned.
- (b) Test every dropdown on `/repo/create` (owner, template, `.gitignore`, licence, labels).

**Rationale:** Since #62 merged, the navbar menus are `<aria-menu>`, and `tests/e2e/menus.test.ts` already drives the avatar menu by keyboard, so (a) would duplicate it. The gap left is a combobox, and the navbar's `aria-haspopup` and `aria-controls`, which only a unit test checks today. (b) multiplies the run time, and the five dropdowns share the same Fomantic code, so one catches what the others would.

**Consequences:** The suite stays under the 2-second target. The other dropdowns on `/repo/create` stay untested end to end; if one diverges later it needs its own test.
```

```text
# Poteto mode

Bundled skills live at `../<name>/SKILL.md` from this file, so put this file's absolute path in every `poteto-agent` prompt.

## Platform Adaptation

These skills use Claude Code tool names (the `Skill` tool, the `Agent` tool, `AskUserQuestion`) and the Claude model names the `Agent` tool accepts, as each Models section lists them. On Claude Code they work as written. On Codex, read [`references/codex-tools.md`](references/codex-tools.md) for the Codex equivalent of a Claude tool, model, or skill named by these workflows. On Pi, read [`references/pi-tools.md`](references/pi-tools.md) instead. On GitHub Copilot, CLI or app, read [`references/copilot-tools.md`](references/copilot-tools.md) instead. Other runtimes can discover the same Agent Skills tree, but they must use their own tool, model, and configuration equivalents. No one of these mappings is a cross-runtime map.

Use the session's task-tracking tools for the todolist. On Claude Code these are `TaskCreate` and `TaskUpdate`, or `TodoWrite` when configured. Availability depends on the model; `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1` enables them through the environment or a project's `.claude/settings.local.json` `env` block. See the [task-tool documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference#task-tool-availability). If no task-tracking tool is available, keep an uncommitted `todo.md` Markdown checklist in the work dir, next to the decision trail, with the playbook steps verbatim and each `skip: <reason>` line. When several sessions share the checkout, name it `.audit/<task-slug>.todo.md`, beside that session's `.audit/<task-slug>.tsv` trail, so they never write one file.

## Non-negotiables

The Principles section below grounds every trigger. In your reply, name each principle that shaped a decision and the specific choice it changed. Cite only principles whose leaf SKILL.md you read this session.

Remaining triggers:

- Nontrivial change, architecture decision, or "are we sure?" → the **how** skill.
- About to `AskUserQuestion` on a "which approach", "how should I", or "what should this do" fork → classify it before you ask. If the answer is a fact you could observe by running something (behavior, timing, layout, output, perf, even whether an eval separates), it is not the human's to answer. Sketch it via the Prototype playbook (`playbooks/prototype.md`) and let the result decide. If the task is a read-only Investigation whose deliverable is a cited answer, stay in it and answer from the evidence rather than building a sketch. Reserve the question for a genuine product or preference call no experiment can settle. Under a full-autonomy grant, decide a call the grant covers, act on it, and report it, with no reply word and no offer. Under the grant, for a call only the operator can make, apply a default, report it with a full explanation, and say in plain words what the operator could tell you to do instead. The operator answers in their own words. Never give a shorthand token to type back. Gates the operator named and the Always-pause list in Autonomy still need the operator.
- Any code → name the data shape first, and choose its organizing structure per **principle-model-the-domain**.
- Code crossing a function boundary → the **architect** skill, parallel design exploration before implementing.
- Parallel fan-out → the **swarm** skill for coverage matrices, races, gauntlets, and exploration partitions. Use **arena** for design or code bakeoffs with base selection and grafting.
- Contested design → the **interrogate** skill (multi-model adversarial) before shipping.
- Nontrivial multi-step → write the throughput checkpoint (Feature step 3).
- Any prose surface, your reply to the user included → the **unslop** skill. Write the reply per **Writing the reply**. Agent-facing prose also follows the **plugin-dev:skill-development** skill (Claude Code's authoring guidance for SKILL.md files).
- Docs, RFCs, readmes, PR descriptions, or commit messages → the **technical-writing** skill (`/technical-writing`), on top of **unslop**.
- Before commit → the **deslop** skill (`/deslop`).
- Before review → the **no-comments** skill (`/no-comments`).
- Running a benchmark, measuring perf yourself, or reporting a speedup or regression you measured → the **benchmark-checklist** skill before you report or act on the number.
- Shipping UI / IDE / CLI → the driver skill. `run` ships with Claude Code and the model can invoke it for CLIs, TUIs, servers, and browser or Electron apps. The bundled `verify` runs only when the user types `/verify`, so for UIs use the project `verify` skill at `.claude/skills/verify/` (generate it with `/create-verification-skill`) and fall back to `run` when the repo has none. For bug fixes, reproduce first on the same surface yourself. Hand to the user only under the narrow Bug fix step 1 exception.
```

```text
    12	- [ ] AC1: Given any page that loads Gitea's main script, with focus outside a text field, when the user presses `?`, then a dialog titled "Keyboard shortcuts" opens with one row for each shortcut in #56's registry on that page (`getShortcuts()`), showing its keys and description.

    35	**Decision:** Build the dialog on the native `<dialog>` element, opened with `showModal()`.

Sibling issue #25 exists to remove Fomantic from the accessibility path, so a new Fomantic modal on an accessibility feature works against it. `showModal()` gives the browser's own focus trap (AC3), Escape to close (AC2), focus return and `aria-modal` semantics, so (b) would mean rewriting behaviour the browser already has, which is the kind of bug #25 is about.

    68	- [ ] AC2: Given shortcuts are turned off, when the user reloads the page or opens another page in the same browser, then they are still off.
    69	- [ ] AC3: Given shortcuts are turned off, when the user presses `?`, then the dialog still opens, so the setting can be turned back on without a mouse.
    70	- [ ] AC4: Given shortcuts are turned off, when the user checks the box again, then `s` on a repository home page focuses the code search box again without a reload.
    71	- [ ] AC5: Given a browser where storage access throws, when a page loads, then shortcuts are on, the checkbox is checked and no uncaught error occurs.
    72	- [ ] AC6: Given shortcuts are turned off, when the user presses `g` and then another key, then no half-finished sequence is kept and neither key runs a shortcut.
    73	- [ ] AC7: Given the page is served in a non-English locale, when the dialog opens, then the checkbox label comes from a locale key.
    74	- [ ] AC8: Unit tests in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` cover AC1, AC3, AC5 and AC6; the e2e test from #57 is extended to cover AC2.
    75	
    76	## Out of Scope
    77	- Remapping shortcuts, or turning off one shortcut at a time.
    78	- Storing the setting on the server or syncing it across browsers.
    79	- A copy of the setting on the user settings pages.
    80	- Keys owned by widgets, such as the code editor and the menus' type-to-jump; #56 already leaves those alone.
    81	
    82	## Open Questions
    83	- WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.4 accepts "turn off", "remap" or "active only on focus". This issue picks "turn off" as the smallest complete option. Reviewer to confirm that reading.
    84	
    85	## Design Decision
    86	**Decision:** Store the setting in the browser with the existing `localUserSettings` wrapper (`web_src/js/modules/user-settings.ts`), under the key `keyboard-shortcuts-enabled` with a default of `true`. The registry's single dispatch point (`handleKeyDown` in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts`) checks it before running any shortcut except `?`.
    87	
    88	**Alternatives Considered:**
    89	- (a) A server-side user setting: a column on the user table and a checkbox on the Appearance settings page.
    90	- (b) The same browser setting, but turning off every shortcut including `?`.
    91	
    92	**Rationale:** (a) needs a migration and a settings form for a preference that belongs to one browser. Someone who uses voice control on one machine does not need shortcuts off everywhere, and a migration costs more than this issue is worth. (b) follows SC 2.1.4 more literally, but a keyboard-only user who turned shortcuts off would have no keyboard way back to the checkbox. That swaps one accessibility failure for another. Keeping exactly one exempt key is the usual way out. `localUserSettings` already wraps every storage call in try/catch, so AC5 needs no new error handling.
    93	
    94	**Consequences:** No server change and no migration. The setting does not follow the user to another browser and support cannot see it. `?` staying live is a deliberate exception, so the check carries a short comment saying why, to stop someone "fixing" it later.
```

```text
     4	As a user replying on an issue or pull request, I want GitHub's `r` shortcut to quote the text I have selected into my reply, or take me straight to the reply box when nothing is selected, so that I can answer a specific point without scrolling to the bottom or opening the comment's menu.

    10	
    11	| When the user presses `r` with | `r` does |
    12	| --- | --- |
    13	| Text selected inside one comment or the description | Quotes it into the reply box and puts the cursor after it |
    14	| Nothing selected, or a selection that is not inside a single comment | Jumps to the reply box |

    19	- [ ] AC2: Given the reply box already has text in it, when the user quotes with `r`, then the existing text is kept and the quote is added after it, separated by a blank line.
    20	- [ ] AC3: Given nothing is selected, or the selection spans more than one comment or lies outside any comment, when the user presses `r`, then the reply box scrolls into view with the cursor at the end of its text, and the text is unchanged.
    21	- [ ] AC4: Given the reply box is showing its Preview tab, when the user presses `r`, then it switches back to Write so the cursor and any quote can be seen.
    22	- [ ] AC5: Given a page with no reply box (an archived repository, a signed-out visitor, or a locked conversation the user cannot comment on), when the user presses `r`, then nothing happens and no error is shown.
    23	- [ ] AC6: Given focus is in the reply box or any other text field, when the user types `r`, then a literal `r` is typed.
    24	- [ ] AC7: Given a page where `r` works, when the shortcuts are listed (`getShortcuts()`, shown by #57's dialog), then `r` has the translated "Quote reply" description and a translated section label for issue and pull request pages.
```

```text
     4	const sequenceTimeoutMs = 1500; // the longest wait between the keys of a sequence
     5	
     6	export type Shortcut = {
     7	  keys: string, // keys pressed one after another, separated by spaces, e.g. "g c"
     8	  description: string, // translated
     9	  section?: string, // translated
    10	  element?: HTMLElement, // the shortcut only exists while this element is in the document
    11	  action: () => void,
    12	};
    13	
    14	export type ShortcutInfo = Pick<Shortcut, 'keys' | 'description' | 'section'>;
    15	
    16	function isActive(shortcut: Shortcut): boolean {
    17	  return !shortcut.element || shortcut.element.isConnected;
    18	}
    19	
    20	// returns the shortcut for exactly these keys, 'prefix' if they start a longer sequence, or null
    21	function matchKeys(shortcuts: Shortcut[], keys: string): Shortcut | 'prefix' | null {
    22	  for (const shortcut of shortcuts) {
    23	    if (shortcut.keys === keys) return shortcut;
    24	    if (shortcut.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `)) return 'prefix';
    25	  }
    26	  return null;
    27	}
    28	
    29	export class ShortcutRegistry {
    30	  shortcuts: Shortcut[] = [];
    31	  pendingKeys = ''; // the start of a sequence pressed so far
    32	  pendingTime = 0;
    33	
    34	  register(shortcut: Shortcut) {
    35	    const keys = shortcut.keys.toLowerCase();
    36	    // a shortcut whose element has left the page, e.g. a hint replaced by file tree navigation, gives way to the new one
    37	    this.shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    38	    const conflict = this.shortcuts.find((s) => s.keys === keys || s.keys.startsWith(`${keys} `) || keys.startsWith(`${s.keys} `));
    39	    if (conflict) throw new Error(`Keyboard shortcut "${keys}" conflicts with "${conflict.keys}"`);
    40	    this.shortcuts.push({...shortcut, keys});
    41	  }
    42	
    43	  list(): ShortcutInfo[] {
    44	    return this.shortcuts.filter(isActive).map(({keys, description, section}) => ({keys, description, section}));
    45	  }
    46	
    47	  handleKeyDown(e: KeyboardEvent) {
    48	    const target = e.target as HTMLElement;
    49	    // the key was already used by a widget such as a menu, or is being typed into a field
    50	    if (e.defaultPrevented || e.ctrlKey || e.metaKey || e.altKey || target.matches('input, textarea, select') || target.isContentEditable) {
    51	      this.pendingKeys = '';
    52	      return;
    53	    }
    54	    if (e.key === 'Shift') return; // not a press of its own, e.g. on the way to "?"
    55	    if (e.repeat) return; // a held key runs its shortcut once, and doesn't start over after a sequence
    56	
    57	    if (Date.now() - this.pendingTime > sequenceTimeoutMs) this.pendingKeys = '';
    58	    const key = e.key.toLowerCase();
    59	    const shortcuts = this.shortcuts.filter(isActive);
    60	    let keys = this.pendingKeys ? `${this.pendingKeys} ${key}` : key;
    61	    let match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    62	    if (!match && keys !== key) {
    63	      // the key does not continue the sequence, so it acts as a fresh press
    64	      keys = key;
    65	      match = matchKeys(shortcuts, keys);
    66	    }
    67	    this.pendingKeys = '';
    68	    if (!match) return;
    69	
    70	    e.preventDefault();
    71	    if (match === 'prefix') {
    72	      this.pendingKeys = keys;
    73	      this.pendingTime = Date.now();
    74	    } else {
    75	      match.action();
    76	    }
    77	  }
    78	}

   129	  document.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
```

```text
    const legacyValue = localStorage?.getItem(legacyKey) ?? null;
    const value = localStorage?.getItem(itemKey) ?? null; // avoid undefined
    if (value !== null && legacyValue !== null) {
      // if both values exist, remove the legacy one
      localStorage?.removeItem(legacyKey);
    } else if (value === null && legacyValue !== null) {
      // migrate legacy value to new key
      localStorage?.removeItem(legacyKey);
      localStorage?.setItem(itemKey, legacyValue);
      return legacyValue;
    }
    return value;
  } catch (e) {
    handleLocalStorageError(e);
  }
  return null;
}

function setLocalStorageUserSetting(settingKey: string, value: string) {
  const legacyKey = settingKey;
  const itemKey = `${itemKeyPrefix}${settingKey}`;
  try {
    localStorage?.removeItem(legacyKey);
    localStorage?.setItem(itemKey, value);
  } catch (e) {
    handleLocalStorageError(e);
  }
}

export const localUserSettings = {
  getString: (key: string, def: string = ''): string => {
    return getLocalStorageUserSetting(key) ?? def;
  },
  setString: (key: string, value: string) => {
    setLocalStorageUserSetting(key, value);
  },
  getBoolean: (key: string, def: boolean = false): boolean => {
    return localUserSettings.getString(key, String(def)) === 'true';
  },
  setBoolean: (key: string, value: boolean) => {
    localUserSettings.setString(key, String(value));
  },
  getJsonObject: <T extends Record<string, any>>(key: string, def: T): T => {
    const value = getLocalStorageUserSetting(key);
    try {
      const decoded = value !== null ? JSON.parse(value) : null;
      return {...def, ...decoded};
    } catch (e) {
      console.error(`Unable to parse JSON value for local user settings ${key}=${value}`, e);
    }
    return def;
  },
  setJsonObject: <T extends Record<string, any>>(key: string, value: T) => {
    localUserSettings.setString(key, JSON.stringify(value));
  },
};

window.localUserSettings = localUserSettings;
```

```text
async function tryOnQuoteReply(e: Event) {
  const clickTarget = (e.target as HTMLElement).closest('.quote-reply');
  if (!clickTarget) return;

  e.preventDefault();
  const contentToQuoteId = clickTarget.getAttribute('data-target');
  const targetRawToQuote = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`#${contentToQuoteId}.raw-content`)!;
  const targetMarkupToQuote = targetRawToQuote.parentElement!.querySelector<HTMLElement>('.render-content.markup')!;
  let contentToQuote = extractSelectedMarkdown(targetMarkupToQuote);
  if (!contentToQuote) contentToQuote = targetRawToQuote.textContent;
  const quotedContent = `${contentToQuote.replace(/^/mg, '> ')}\n\n`;

  let editor;
  if (clickTarget.classList.contains('quote-reply-diff')) {
    const replyBtn = clickTarget.closest('.comment-code-cloud')!.querySelector<HTMLElement>('button.comment-form-reply')!;
    editor = await handleReply(replyBtn);
  } else {
    // for normal issue/comment page
    editor = getComboMarkdownEditor(document.querySelector('#comment-form .combo-markdown-editor'))!;
  }

  if (editor.value()) {
    editor.value(`${editor.value()}\n\n${quotedContent}`);
  } else {
    editor.value(quotedContent);
  }
  editor.focus();
  editor.moveCursorToEnd();
}

export function initRepoIssueCommentEdit() {
  document.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    tryOnEditContent(e); // Edit issue or comment content
    tryOnQuoteReply(e); // Quote reply to the comment editor
  });
}
```

```text
import {hideElem, querySingleVisibleElem, showElem, toggleElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';
import {htmlEscape} from '../utils/html.ts';
import {fomanticQuery} from '../modules/fomantic/base.ts';
import {sanitizeRepoName} from './repo-common.ts';

const {appSubUrl} = window.config;

function initRepoNewTemplateSearch(form: HTMLFormElement) {
  const elSubmitButton = querySingleVisibleElem<HTMLInputElement>(form, '.ui.primary.button')!;
  const elCreateRepoErrorMessage = form.querySelector('#create-repo-error-message')!;
  const elRepoOwnerDropdown = form.querySelector('#repo_owner_dropdown')!;
  const elRepoTemplateDropdown = form.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('#repo_template_search')!;
  const inputRepoTemplate = form.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('#repo_template')!;
  const elTemplateUnits = form.querySelector('#template_units')!;
  const elNonTemplate = form.querySelector('#non_template')!;
  const checkTemplate = function () {
    const hasSelectedTemplate = inputRepoTemplate.value !== '' && inputRepoTemplate.value !== '0';
    toggleElem(elTemplateUnits, hasSelectedTemplate);
    toggleElem(elNonTemplate, !hasSelectedTemplate);
  };
  inputRepoTemplate.addEventListener('change', checkTemplate);
  checkTemplate();

  const $repoOwnerDropdown = fomanticQuery(elRepoOwnerDropdown);
  const $repoTemplateDropdown = fomanticQuery(elRepoTemplateDropdown);
  const onChangeOwner = function () {
    const ownerId = $repoOwnerDropdown.dropdown('get value');
    const $ownerItem = $repoOwnerDropdown.dropdown('get item', ownerId);
    hideElem(elCreateRepoErrorMessage);
    elSubmitButton.disabled = false;
    if ($ownerItem?.length) {
      const elOwnerItem = $ownerItem[0];
      elCreateRepoErrorMessage.textContent = elOwnerItem.getAttribute('data-create-repo-disallowed-prompt') ?? '';
      const hasError = Boolean(elCreateRepoErrorMessage.textContent);
      toggleElem(elCreateRepoErrorMessage, hasError);
      elSubmitButton.disabled = hasError;
    }
    $repoTemplateDropdown.dropdown('setting', {
      apiSettings: {
        url: `${appSubUrl}/repo/search?q={query}&template=true&priority_owner_id=${ownerId}`,
        onResponse(response: any) {
          const results = [];
          results.push({name: '', value: ''}); // empty item means not using template
          for (const tmplRepo of response.data) {
            results.push({
              name: htmlEscape(tmplRepo.repository.full_name),
              value: String(tmplRepo.repository.id),
            });
          }
          return {results};
        },
        cache: false,
      },
    });
  };
  $repoOwnerDropdown.dropdown('setting', 'onChange', onChangeOwner);
  onChangeOwner();
}
```

```text
// for static dropdown elements (generated by server-side template), prepare them with necessary aria attributes
function attachStaticElements(dropdown: HTMLElement, focusable: HTMLElement, menu: HTMLElement) {
  // prepare static dropdown menu list popup
  if (!menu.id) {
    menu.id = generateElemId('_aria_dropdown_menu_');
  }

  $(menu).find('> .item, > .scrolling.menu > .item').each((_, item) => updateMenuItem(dropdown, item));

  // this role could only be changed after its content is ready, otherwise some browsers+readers (like Chrome+AppleVoice) crash
  menu.setAttribute('role', (dropdown as any)[ariaPatchKey].listPopupRole);
  if (dropdown.classList.contains('multiple')) menu.setAttribute('aria-multiselectable', 'true');
  refreshAriaSelected(dropdown);

  // prepare selection label items
  for (const label of dropdown.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('.ui.label')) {
    updateSelectionLabel(label);
  }

  // make the primary element (focusable) aria-friendly
  focusable.setAttribute('role', focusable.getAttribute('role') ?? (dropdown as any)[ariaPatchKey].focusableRole);
  focusable.setAttribute('aria-haspopup', (dropdown as any)[ariaPatchKey].listPopupRole);
  focusable.setAttribute('aria-controls', menu.id);
  focusable.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');

  // use tooltip's content as aria-label if there is no aria-label
  const tooltipContent = dropdown.getAttribute('data-tooltip-content');
  if (tooltipContent && !dropdown.getAttribute('aria-label')) {
    dropdown.setAttribute('aria-label', tooltipContent);
  }

  //    - otherwise, the dropdown control (low-level code) handles the Enter event, hides the dropdown menu

  // TODO: multiple selection is only partially supported. Check and test them one by one in the future.

  const textSearch = dropdown.querySelector<HTMLElement>('input.search');
  const focusable = textSearch || dropdown; // the primary element for focus, see comment above
  if (!focusable) return;

  // as a combobox, the input should not have autocomplete by default
  if (textSearch && !textSearch.getAttribute('autocomplete')) {
    textSearch.setAttribute('autocomplete', 'off');
  }

  let menu = $(dropdown).find('> .menu')[0];
  if (!menu) {
    // some "multiple selection" dropdowns don't have a static menu element in HTML, we need to pre-create it to make it have correct aria attributes
    menu = document.createElement('div');
    menu.classList.add('menu');
    dropdown.append(menu);
  }

  // There are 2 possible solutions about the role: combobox or menu.
  // The idea is that if there is an input, then it's a combobox, otherwise it's a menu.
  // Since #19861 we have prepared the "combobox" solution, but didn't get enough time to put it into practice and test before.
  const isComboBox = dropdown.querySelectorAll('input').length > 0;

  (dropdown as any)[ariaPatchKey].focusableRole = isComboBox ? 'combobox' : 'menu';
  (dropdown as any)[ariaPatchKey].listPopupRole = isComboBox ? 'listbox' : '';
  (dropdown as any)[ariaPatchKey].listItemRole = isComboBox ? 'option' : 'menuitem';

  attachDomEvents(dropdown, focusable, menu);
  attachStaticElements(dropdown, focusable, menu);
}

function attachDomEvents(dropdown: HTMLElement, focusable: HTMLElement, menu: HTMLElement) {
  // when showing, it has class: ".animating.in"
  // when hiding, it has class: ".visible.animating.out"
  const isMenuVisible = () => (menu.classList.contains('visible') && !menu.classList.contains('out')) || menu.classList.contains('in');

  // update aria attributes according to current active/selected item
  const refreshAriaActiveItem = () => {
    const menuVisible = isMenuVisible();
    focusable.setAttribute('aria-expanded', menuVisible ? 'true' : 'false');

    // if there is an active item, use it (the user is navigating between items)
    // otherwise use the "selected" for combobox (for the last selected item)
    const active = $(menu).find('> .item.active, > .item.selected, > .scrolling.menu > .item.selected')[0];
    if (!active) return;
    // if the popup is visible and has an active/selected item, use its id as aria-activedescendant
    if (menuVisible) {
      focusable.setAttribute('aria-activedescendant', active.id);
    } else if ((dropdown as any)[ariaPatchKey].listPopupRole === 'menu') {
      // for menu, when the popup is hidden, no need to keep the aria-activedescendant, and clear the active/selected item
      focusable.removeAttribute('aria-activedescendant');
      active.classList.remove('active', 'selected');
    }
  };

  dropdown.addEventListener('keydown', (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
    if (e.isComposing) return;
    // here it must use keydown event before dropdown's keyup handler, otherwise there is no Enter event in our keyup handler
    if (e.key === 'Enter') {
      const elItem = menu.querySelector<HTMLElement>(':scope > .item.selected, .menu > .item.selected');
      // if the selected item is clickable, then trigger the click event.
      // we can not click any item without check, because Fomantic code might also handle the Enter event. that would result in double click.
      if (elItem?.matches('a, .js-aria-clickable') && !elItem.matches('.tw-hidden, .filtered')) {
        e.preventDefault();
        elItem.click();
      }
    }
  });

  // use setTimeout to run the refreshAria in next tick (to make sure the Fomantic UI code has finished its work)
  // do not return any value, jQuery has return-value related behaviors.
  // when the popup is hiding, it's better to have a small "delay", because there is a Fomantic UI animation
  // without the delay for hiding, the UI will be somewhat laggy and sometimes may get stuck in the animation.
  const deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem = (delay = 0) => { setTimeout(refreshAriaActiveItem, delay) };
  (dropdown as any)[ariaPatchKey].deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem = deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem;
  dropdown.addEventListener('keyup', (e) => { if (e.key.startsWith('Arrow')) deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem(); });

  // if the dropdown has been opened by focus, do not trigger the next click event again.
  // otherwise the dropdown will be closed immediately, especially on Android with TalkBack
  // * desktop event sequence: mousedown -> focus -> mouseup -> click
  // * mobile event sequence: focus -> mousedown -> mouseup -> click
  // Fomantic may stop propagation of blur event, use capture to make sure we can still get the event
  let ignoreClickPreEvents = 0, ignoreClickPreVisible = 0;
```

```text
import type {FomanticInitFunction} from '../../types.ts';
import {generateElemId, queryElems} from '../../utils/dom.ts';
import {announceSelectionChange} from '../aria-announce.ts';

const ariaPatchKey = '_giteaAriaPatchDropdown';
const fomanticDropdownFn = $.fn.dropdown;

// use our own `$().dropdown` function to patch Fomantic's dropdown module
export function initAriaDropdownPatch() {
  if ($.fn.dropdown === ariaDropdownFn) throw new Error('initAriaDropdownPatch could only be called once');
  $.fn.dropdown = ariaDropdownFn;
  $.fn.fomanticExt.onDropdownAfterFiltered = onDropdownAfterFiltered;
  (ariaDropdownFn as FomanticInitFunction).settings = fomanticDropdownFn.settings;
}

// the patched `$.fn.dropdown` function, it passes the arguments to Fomantic's `$.fn.dropdown` function, and:
// * it does the one-time element event attaching on the first call
// * it delegates the module internal functions like `onLabelCreate` to the patched functions to add more features.
function ariaDropdownFn(this: any, ...args: Parameters<FomanticInitFunction>) {
  const ret = fomanticDropdownFn.apply(this, args);

  for (let el of this) {
    // dropdown will replace '<select class="ui dropdown"/>' to '<div class="ui dropdown"><select (hidden)></select><div class="menu">...</div></div>'
    // so we need to correctly find the closest '.ui.dropdown' element, it is the real fomantic dropdown module.
    el = el.closest('.ui.dropdown');
    if (!el[ariaPatchKey]) {
      // the elements don't belong to the dropdown "module" and won't be reset
      // so we only need to initialize them once.
      attachInitElements(el);
    }

    // if the `$().dropdown()` is called without arguments, or it has non-string (object) argument,
    // it means that such call will reset the dropdown "module" including internal settings,
    // then we need to re-delegate the callbacks.
    const $dropdown = $(el);
    const dropdownModule = $dropdown.data('module-dropdown');
    if (!dropdownModule.giteaDelegated) {
      dropdownModule.giteaDelegated = true;
      delegateDropdownModule($dropdown);
    }
  }
  return ret;
}

  item.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
  for (const el of item.querySelectorAll('a, input, button')) el.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
}
```

```text
  let ignoreClickPreEvents = 0, ignoreClickPreVisible = 0;
  dropdown.addEventListener('mousedown', () => {
    ignoreClickPreVisible += isMenuVisible() ? 1 : 0;
    ignoreClickPreEvents++;
  }, {capture: true});
  dropdown.addEventListener('focus', () => {
    ignoreClickPreVisible += isMenuVisible() ? 1 : 0;
    ignoreClickPreEvents++;
    deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem();
  }, {capture: true});
  dropdown.addEventListener('blur', () => {
    ignoreClickPreVisible = ignoreClickPreEvents = 0;
    deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem(100);
  }, {capture: true});
  dropdown.addEventListener('mouseup', () => {
    setTimeout(() => {
      ignoreClickPreVisible = ignoreClickPreEvents = 0;
      deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem(100);
    }, 0);
  }, {capture: true});
  dropdown.addEventListener('click', (e: MouseEvent) => {
    if (isMenuVisible() &&
      ignoreClickPreVisible !== 2 && // dropdown is switch from invisible to visible
      ignoreClickPreEvents === 2 // the click event is related to mousedown+focus
    ) {
      e.stopPropagation(); // if the dropdown menu has been opened by focus, do not trigger the next click event again
    }
    ignoreClickPreEvents = ignoreClickPreVisible = 0;
  }, {capture: true});
}
```

```text
`?` opens a shortcut help dialog built from the registry
enhancement,scope: medium
Sprint 2
controlled-opposition
> Sub-issue of #23 · **P1** · estimate **5 points** (medium) · blocked by #56

## User Story
As a user who suspects Gitea has keyboard shortcuts but cannot find them, I want to press `?` on
any page and see every available shortcut grouped by area, so that I can learn them without
reading the source or the docs.

## User Scenario
A user is looking at an issue. They press `?`. A dialog opens in the centre of the page titled
"Keyboard shortcuts", listing the shortcuts under headings such as "Site-wide" and "Repository",
each row showing the keys as `<kbd>` elements next to a description. Focus moves into the dialog;
Tab cycles inside it and does not reach the page behind. They press Escape, the dialog closes, and
focus returns to where it was.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given any page with focus on the document body, when the user presses `?`, then a
      dialog opens listing one row per shortcut registered in #56, with the keys and the
      description.
- [ ] AC2: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses Escape, then it closes and focus
      returns to the element that was focused before it opened.
- [ ] AC3: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses Tab repeatedly, then focus stays inside
      the dialog and never lands on a control on the page behind it.
- [ ] AC4: Given focus is in a comment textarea, when the user types `?`, then a literal `?` is
      inserted and the dialog does not open.
- [ ] AC5: Given a new shortcut is registered with a descr
=== 60
Character-key shortcuts can be turned off (WCAG 2.1.4)
enhancement,scope: small
Sprint 2
controlled-opposition
> Sub-issue of #23 · **P3 — Sprint 2 carryover** · estimate **2 points** (small) · blocked by #56, #57

## User Story
As a user of speech recognition software, I want to turn off Gitea's single-character shortcuts,
so that dictating a word into the page does not fire a shortcut and navigate me away from what I
was writing.

## User Scenario
Someone using voice control finds that saying a word while the page has focus keeps triggering the
file finder. They press `?`, see a checkbox at the bottom of the shortcut dialog reading "Enable
character key shortcuts", and clear it. The shortcut list greys out. They close the dialog, dictate
freely, and the setting is still off the next time they open Gitea in that browser.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given the shortcut help dialog, when the user clears the "Enable character key
      shortcuts" checkbox, then pressing `s`, `t` or any `g` sequence has no effect.
- [ ] AC2: Given shortcuts are disabled, when the user reloads the page, then they are still
      disabled.
- [ ] AC3: Given shortcuts are disabled, when the user presses `?`, then the help dialog still
      opens, so the setting can be turned back on without a mouse.
- [ ] AC4: Given shortcuts are disabled, when the user re-checks the box, then `s` focuses the
      repo sidebar search again without a reload.
- [ ] AC5: Given a browser with storage blocked, when the page loads, then shortcuts default to
      enabled and no error is thrown.

=== 95
`r` quotes selected text into the reply box on issue and pull request pages
enhancement,scope: small
Sprint 2
controlled-opposition
## User Story

As a user replying on an issue or pull request, I want GitHub's `r` shortcut to quote the text I have selected into my reply, or take me straight to the reply box when nothing is selected, so that I can answer a specific point without scrolling to the bottom or opening the comment's menu.

## User Scenario
A maintainer is reading a long issue thread. They select a sentence in someone's comment and press `r`. The page scrolls to the reply box at the bottom, the sentence is already in it as a Markdown quote, and the cursor sits after it, ready to type. Later, back at the top of the thread with nothing selected, they press `r` again and land in the same reply box with their text still there.

On a page with no reply box, such as an archived repository or when signed out, `r` does nothing.

| When the user presses `r` with | `r` does |
| --- | --- |
| Text selected inside one comment | Quotes it into the reply box and puts the cursor after it |
| Nothing selected, or a selection that is not inside a single comment | Jumps to the reply box |
| No reply box on the page | Nothing |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given text is selected inside a comment or the issue description on an issue or pull request page, when the user presses `r`, then the text is added to the reply box as a Markdown quote, the box scrolls into view, and the cursor is placed after the quote.
- [ ] AC2: Given the reply box already has text in it, when the user quotes with `r`, then the existin
=== 65
Playwright keyboard regression suite for dropdowns
enhancement,scope: small
Sprint 2
controlled-opposition
> Sub-issue of #25 · **P1** · estimate **2 points** (small) · blocked by nothing

## User Story
As a contributor changing dropdown code, I want an end-to-end test that fails when keyboard
operation or the ARIA attributes break, so that the accessibility work in this sprint is not
quietly undone by a later refactor.

## User Scenario
A contributor opens a PR that changes `dropdown.ts`. CI runs the new suite: it Tabs to the navbar
profile dropdown, checks `aria-expanded` flips to `true`, arrows down, checks
`aria-activedescendant` points at an element that exists, presses Escape and checks focus is back
on the trigger. Their change had dropped the `aria-controls` attribute; the suite fails and names
which assertion.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: A new `tests/e2e/` spec covers, for the signed-in navbar profile dropdown: Tab to it,
      open by keyboard, arrow between items, activate with Enter, and close with Escape.
- [ ] AC2: The spec asserts `aria-expanded` is `false` when closed and `true` when open.
- [ ] AC3: The spec asserts that while open, `aria-activedescendant` resolves to an element that
      exists in the document and is an item of that dropdown.
- [ ] AC4: The spec asserts the trigger's `aria-haspopup` and `aria-controls`, and that
      `aria-controls` resolves to the popup.
- [ ] AC5: After Escape, the spec asserts focus is on the trigger.
- [ ] AC6: The spec calls `assertNoJsError` from `tests/e2e/utils.ts` and completes in under 2
      seconds locally,
```
