> Sub-issue of #25 · **P1** · estimate **2 points** (small) · blocked by nothing

## User Story
As a contributor changing dropdown code, I want end-to-end tests that fail when a dropdown's ARIA state stops matching what the keyboard user sees, so that the accessibility work from Sprint 1 is not quietly undone by a later refactor.

## User Scenario
A contributor opens a PR that changes `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts`. CI runs the label picker test on an issue page. It opens the picker from the keyboard, checks that `aria-expanded` flips to `true`, presses ArrowDown, checks that `aria-activedescendant` names one of the picker's options, then presses Escape and checks the list closed. Their change had dropped `aria-controls`, so the test fails and names that assertion.

A second contributor changes `<aria-menu>` and drops `aria-haspopup` from the navbar avatar menu. The navbar test fails and names it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given a signed-in user on an issue with seeded labels, when the test opens the sidebar label picker from the keyboard, then it asserts the picker's search input has role `combobox`, `aria-expanded` is `false` before opening and `true` after, and `aria-controls` names the picker's list.
- [ ] AC2: Given the label picker is open, when the test presses ArrowDown, then it asserts `aria-activedescendant` names an element that exists and has role `option` inside that list.
- [ ] AC3: Given the label picker is open, when the test presses Escape, then it asserts the list is hidden, focus is still on the picker's input, and `aria-expanded` is `false`.
- [ ] AC4: Given the signed-in navbar, then `tests/e2e/menus.test.ts` asserts that each `<aria-menu>` trigger has `aria-haspopup="menu"` and that its `aria-controls` names an element with role `menu`.
- [ ] AC5: Each new or extended test calls `assertNoJsError` from `tests/e2e/utils.ts` and finishes in under 2 seconds locally.
- [ ] AC6: The tests run with `GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='<the test file>' make test-e2e`. Every assertion passes on `main`, except one that finds a bug, which is marked `test.fail` with a link to a new issue for that bug (see Out of Scope).

## Out of Scope
- Fixing what the tests find. A failing assertion gets a new bug issue and a `test.fail` marker linking it, so the suite records the bug and starts failing once it is fixed. Product code does not change here.
- Navbar keyboard behaviour already covered by `tests/e2e/menus.test.ts` and `tests/e2e/aria-menu.test.ts` (open, arrow keys, Home/End, Escape, type to jump).
- The `aria-selected` and label announcement checks already in `tests/e2e/multiselect-aria.test.ts`.
- Adding `axe-core` or any other accessibility-testing dependency.
- Covering every Fomantic dropdown.
- Screen reader output, which no automated test can check.

## Open Questions
- Reading `dropdown.ts` suggests Escape does not refresh `aria-expanded` (it is refreshed on focus, blur, mouseup and arrow-key keyup only), so AC3's last check may fail on `main`. The first step of the implementation is to run it and, if it fails, file the bug as AC6 describes.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: what kind of test
**Decision:** Assert the ARIA attributes and focus position directly in Playwright.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Add `@axe-core/playwright` and assert the page has no violations.
- (b) Add the checks to the vitest unit tests in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.test.ts`, which already start real Fomantic dropdowns in happy-dom.

**Rationale:** (a) adds a dependency and reports on the page's markup in general rather than on the state a keyboard user depends on. It would not catch `aria-activedescendant` pointing at the wrong option, and an axe failure elsewhere on the page would fail the test for unrelated reasons. (b) can check static attributes, but the bugs this suite guards against happen in real key sequences: `dropdown.ts` refreshes the ARIA state on a timer after keyup, and the picker's open and close run through Fomantic's animation. The unit tests would have to fake the timing they are meant to check.

**Consequences:** A failing assertion names the exact attribute that broke. The assertions depend on today's Fomantic markup, so moving the label picker off Fomantic (under #25) will need this test updated, and the test carries a comment saying so.

### Decision 2: which dropdowns to test
**Decision:** Extend `tests/e2e/multiselect-aria.test.ts` with the `aria-expanded`, `aria-activedescendant` and `aria-controls` checks on the issue label picker, and add the `aria-haspopup` and `aria-controls` checks to the existing navbar test.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Write a full keyboard suite for the navbar avatar menu, as the first draft of this issue planned.
- (b) A new test for the repository template search on `/repo/create`.

**Rationale:** Since #62 merged, the navbar menus are `<aria-menu>`, and `tests/e2e/menus.test.ts` already drives the avatar menu by keyboard, so (a) would mostly repeat it. (b) tests a combobox too, but its options load from the API after the menu opens, which adds waits and makes the test slower and less stable. The label picker has the same combobox role, its labels are seeded by the test, and `multiselect-aria.test.ts` already opens it, so the new checks are a few lines on an existing path.

**Consequences:** The suite stays under the 2-second target and adds no new test file. Search dropdowns that load from the API, like the template search, stay untested end to end.

## Scope
small (2 points)

function attachDomEvents(dropdown: HTMLElement, focusable: HTMLElement, menu: HTMLElement) {
  // when showing, it has class: ".animating.in"
  // when hiding, it has class: ".visible.animating.out"
  const isMenuVisible = () => (menu.classList.contains('visible') && !menu.classList.contains('out')) || menu.classList.contains('in');

  // update aria attributes according to current active/selected item
  const refreshAriaActiveItem = () => {
    const menuVisible = isMenuVisible();
    focusable.setAttribute('aria-expanded', menuVisible ? 'true' : 'false');

    // if there is an active item, use it (the user is navigating between items)
    // otherwise use the "selected" for combobox (for the last selected item)
    const active = $(menu).find('> .item.active, > .item.selected, > .scrolling.menu > .item.selected')[0];
    if (!active) return;
    // if the popup is visible and has an active/selected item, use its id as aria-activedescendant
    if (menuVisible) {
      focusable.setAttribute('aria-activedescendant', active.id);
    } else if ((dropdown as any)[ariaPatchKey].listPopupRole === 'menu') {
      // for menu, when the popup is hidden, no need to keep the aria-activedescendant, and clear the active/selected item
      focusable.removeAttribute('aria-activedescendant');
      active.classList.remove('active', 'selected');
    }

s=s[:start]+'''## Design Decision

### Decision 1: where the setting is stored
**Decision:** Store it in the browser with the existing `localUserSettings` wrapper (`web_src/js/modules/user-settings.ts`), under the key `keyboard-shortcuts-enabled` with a default of `true`. The registry's single dispatch point (`handleKeyDown` in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts`) checks it before running a shortcut.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) A per-user server setting in the existing `user_setting` key-value table (`models/user/setting.go`), with a checkbox on the Appearance settings page.
- (b) A cookie read by the server, which would leave shortcut registration out of the page altogether when they are off.

**Rationale:** Shortcuts also work for signed-out visitors, and (a) has nowhere to store their choice. The preference also belongs to one setup: someone who uses voice control on one machine does not need shortcuts off everywhere. (b) would let the server skip the hints, but it sends the setting with every request and needs a server change for what is a browser-only behaviour. `localUserSettings` already wraps every storage call in try/catch, so AC5 needs no new error handling.

**Consequences:** No server change. The setting does not follow the user to another browser and support cannot see it.

### Decision 2: which keys the setting covers
**Decision:** Turn off every character shortcut except `?`.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Turn off every shortcut, `?` included, which reads SC 2.1.4 most literally.
- (b) Use SC 2.1.4's other accepted option, "active only on focus", so shortcuts run only while focus is on a particular component.

**Rationale:** (a) leaves a keyboard-only user who turned shortcuts off with no keyboard way back to the checkbox, which swaps one accessibility failure for another. One exempt key is the usual escape hatch. (b) fits a widget's own keys, but Gitea's shortcuts act on the whole page (`s` jumps to search from anywhere), so restricting them to one component would remove what they are for.

# Technical writing

Write so a tired engineer understands on the first read. Apply all four layers.

Three rules sit above the layers:

- **Cut every word that does no work.** If the sentence survives without a word, the word goes. "In order to" is "to". "It is important to note that" is nothing.
- **Use the short, everyday word.** "Use", not "utilize". "Help", not "facilitate". "Do", not "perform". A long word has to buy its length with precision.
- **When a rule makes a sentence worse, fix the sentence another way or leave it alone.** A sentence that follows every rule and sounds like a machine wrote it has failed.

The codebase is the word list. Write the real symbol, file, flag, or command name, not a synonym or a description of it.

Don't invent jargon. Use the words a developer would say out loud: "move", "delete", "a budget that only decreases", not "evacuate", "ratchet", or "endgame". A named pattern is fine when the doc says what it means the first time. Propose a new offender and its replacement as an addition to `unslop`'s abstract-metaphor rule in your reply, with the diff. Don't edit that skill.

## Vary the rhythm

A doc can obey every layer and still read machine-written: every sentence clipped short, no view anywhere, nothing specific.

- Mix sentence lengths on purpose. Short sentences land a point. Longer ones carry a fact with its condition or consequence.
- One thought per sentence does not mean one length per sentence. Split the sentence that carries two thoughts. Keep the long sentence that carries one.
- Have a view where the mode allows it. Explanation weighs trade-offs, so say what you make of them instead of listing pros and cons. Reference stays dry.
- Be specific over sterile. Not "schema changes can cause issues" but "a column rename fails the build".

## Pick the mode first (Diátaxis)

One document, one mode. Two questions pick it: does the content inform action (doing) or understanding (thinking), and does it serve learning or work?

- Action + learning: **tutorial**.
- Action + work: **how-to**.
- Understanding + work: **reference**.
- Understanding + learning: **explanation**.

Use the compass on a whole document or on one sentence.

**Tutorial: learning by doing.** The learner's success is your job, not theirs. Open by saying what the learner will build, not what they will "learn". Every step produces a visible result, early and often. Tell them what they should see: the expected output, the prompt change, the log line. Cut explanation to one clause and a link. Stay concrete. Write as "we", in commands: "First, do x. Now, do y."

**How-to: steps to a goal.** Solve a problem a person has, not an operation the machine can perform. Assume competence and skip teaching. Action only: no digressions, no background, no completeness for its own sake. Link those instead. Allow forks and judgment: "If you want x, do y." Name the guide by the task: "How to calibrate the radar array", not "Radar array calibration".

**Reference: facts for lookup.** Only describe. No instruction, no persuasion, no opinion. Be dry, complete, and sure. State facts, options, limits, and errors with no hedging. Mirror the structure of the thing described, so code and docs can be navigated together. Put material where readers expect it. Generate from code where possible.

**Explanation: understanding and why.** One bounded topic, readable away from the product. Each title should tolerate an implicit "About..." in front. Anchor on a real why question. Give context: design decisions, history, constraints, alternatives. Opinion is allowed here and nowhere else.

Don't mix modes: no reference tables inside a tutorial, no tutorial hand-holding inside reference, no arguing inside a how-to. Split and link instead.

## Write sentences to the reader (Google developer style)

- Talk to the reader as "you", in the present tense. "Will" only for things that genuinely happen later.
- Say who does what: "the compiler checks", not "is checked". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or beside the point.
- Write instructions as commands: "Click Submit." State facts plainly. Never "should be done".
- Put the condition before the instruction: "To delete the document, click Delete."
- Put the common case first. Exceptions after.
- Sound like a knowledgeable friend. No buzzwords, no figurative language, no "please" in instructions, and never "simply", "easy", or "quickly" in a procedure. If it were simple, the reader would not be here.
- Don't pre-announce ("we will soon support...") and don't start consecutive sentences with the same phrase.
- Link with words that say where the link goes: the page title or a short description. Never "click here". Prefer a sentence of context on the page over a link off it.
- Headings carry the point, not just the topic ("Pick the mode first", not "Modes"). Sentence case. A task heading is a bare verb phrase ("Create an instance"). A concept heading is a noun phrase. One h1 per page, no skipped levels.
- Numbered lists for sequences, bullets for everything else. Introduce a list with a complete sentence. Keep items parallel.
- Code goes in code font. UI elements go in bold. Use serial commas. Drop "etc." and say up front that a list is partial.

## Make statements load one at a time (STE rules)

- One instruction per sentence. One thought per sentence everywhere else.
- Split instructions longer than about 20 words and other sentences longer than about 25.
- Put the warning or condition before the step it guards: "If hot oil touches your skin, injuries can occur."
- Keep "the" and "a": "Remove backup file" reads two ways. "Remove the backup file" reads one.
- Give each word one meaning and one job, then keep it. If "check" means inspect, don't also use it for restrain.
- Pick one word per action and stick to it: "start", not "start" here and "initiate" there.
- Write procedures as direct commands, never as narration and never in the passive: "Install the component", not "the component must be installed".
- Avoid "-ing" words where you can.

## Leave no sentence open to two readings (Global English)

- Keep words like "only" and "not" next to the word they change: "only fails on growth" and "fails only on growth" say different things.
- Break up long noun strings: "the proto import budget check script" becomes "the script that checks the proto-import budget".
- Make every "it", "they", and "this" point at one obvious thing. Repeat the noun when in doubt. Never use "this" or "which" to point at a whole clause.
- Don't drop verbs: "Phase 1 moves the converters and Phase 2 the runtime" leaves Phase 2 without one. Give it one.
- Keep the small words that show structure, such as "that" in "Ensure that the switch is off". Never trade clarity for word count.
- Repeat the article in a series when it prevents a misread: "the client and the host", not "the client and host", when they are two things.
- Say which parts "and" or "or" joins when a sentence can group two ways. "Both...and", "either...or", and "if...then" are free disambiguators.
- Use periods, not semicolons. Replace an em dash with a new sentence.
- Make text in parentheses a full grammatical unit or its own sentence. Never form plurals with "(s)".
- No slashes: write "a, b, or both" instead of "a/b" or "and/or".
- Call each thing by one name, everywhere. A doc that says "the gate", "the ratchet", and "the budget check" for one thing teaches three things. Don't churn what didn't change.
- Skip idioms, colloquialisms, Latin abbreviations, and metaphors.

## Voice and repo specifics

- Apply the **unslop** skill to every doc this skill touches. That skill owns the slop-pattern catalog: AI vocabulary, filler, hedging, formatting tells.
- PR descriptions and commit messages are writing too. Every layer except Diátaxis applies to them. A PR body is a briefing that a reviewer can read in under a minute. Do not paste swarm logs, SHA lists, or metric tables. Link them.
- Product UI strings are not documentation. Use your product's copy guidelines for those.
- Indent code snippets with tabs. Write real paths. Make every count or tree claim true at the commit that lands it, and include the command that regenerates it.

## Worked example

Before:

> Configuration of the proto import ratchet budget script parameters is performed via budget.json. Note that it's important to remember that running with --write, which updates the committed budget to reflect the current count, should only be done when lowering it. If exceeded, CI fails.

After:

> `budget.mjs` reads the committed budget from `budget.json` and counts the files that import protos. If the count exceeds the budget, CI fails. Run `budget.mjs --write` only to lower the budget.

> Sub-issue of #23 · **P1** · estimate **5 points** (medium) · blocked by #56

## User Story
As a keyboard user who suspects Gitea has shortcuts but cannot find them, I want to press `?` on any page and see the shortcuts that work on that page, grouped by section, so that I can learn them without reading the source or the docs.

## User Scenario
A user is on a repository's home page. They press `?`. A dialog titled "Keyboard shortcuts" opens in the middle of the page. It lists `?` under "General", and `S` ("Search code…") and `T` ("Go to file") under "Repository", each row showing the keys as `<kbd>` elements next to the description. Focus moves into the dialog, and Tab cycles inside it without reaching the page behind. They press Escape. The dialog closes and focus returns to where it was.

On their notifications page, which has no page-specific shortcuts, `?` opens the same dialog listing only `?`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given any page that loads Gitea's main script, with focus outside a text field, when the user presses `?`, then a dialog titled "Keyboard shortcuts" opens with one row for each shortcut in #56's registry on that page (`getShortcuts()`), showing its keys and description.
- [ ] AC2: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses Escape, then it closes and focus returns to the element that was focused before it opened.
- [ ] AC3: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses Tab repeatedly, then focus never reaches a control on the page behind it.
- [ ] AC4: Given focus is in an input, textarea or editable area, when the user types `?`, then a literal `?` is typed and the dialog does not open.
- [ ] AC5: Given shortcuts with different section labels, when the dialog opens, then each section is a heading with its shortcuts under it. A shortcut registered later with a new section appears under that section with no change to the dialog's code.
- [ ] AC6: Given the page is served in a non-English locale, when the dialog opens, then its title, its close button's accessible name and the "General" section come from locale keys, not hard-coded English.
- [ ] AC7: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses `?` again, then the dialog stays open as it is and no error occurs.
- [ ] AC8: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses a key that is another shortcut on the page (for example `s` on a repository home page), then that shortcut does not run.
- [ ] AC9: A Playwright test in `tests/e2e/` covers AC1, AC2, AC4 and AC8 on a repository home page and calls `assertNoJsError`; unit tests in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` cover the grouping in AC5.

## Out of Scope
- Adding shortcuts other than `?` itself. The `g` shortcuts are #58, `c` is #59 and `r` is #95; each appears in the dialog once it is registered.
- Listing shortcuts that belong to other pages. The dialog shows what works on the current page.
- Editing or remapping a shortcut from the dialog.
- The setting to turn shortcuts off. That is #60, which adds a checkbox to this dialog.
- A link to the dialog in the footer or a menu, and a printable or documentation page of shortcuts.

## Open Questions
- Should the dialog also be reachable by mouse, for example from a footer link? Proposed: not in this issue, so there is one entry point and the e2e test covers it.
- Should a click on the backdrop close the dialog? Proposed: no, so Escape and the close button are the only ways out. Reviewer to confirm.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: the dialog element
**Decision:** Build the dialog on the native `<dialog>` element, opened with `showModal()`.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) A Fomantic modal shown with `showFomanticModal` from `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/modal.ts`, which is what Gitea's other modals use today.
- (b) A plain `<div>` with a hand-written focus trap, backdrop and Escape handler.

**Rationale:** `.claude-students/docs/frontend-js.md` says Fomantic is deprecated and new features must not be built on it. Sibling issue #25 exists to remove Fomantic from the accessibility path, so a new Fomantic modal on an accessibility feature works against it. `showModal()` makes the page behind inert (AC3), closes on Escape (AC2) and gives `aria-modal` semantics, so (b) would mean rewriting behaviour the browser already has, which is the kind of bug #25 is about.

**Consequences:** AC2 and AC3 come mostly from the browser, and the dialog has no jQuery dependency. Browsers differ on returning focus when a dialog closes, so the close handler restores focus itself. #56's registry listens on the whole document, so the dialog stops other shortcuts while it is open (AC8). It is the first native `<dialog>` in Gitea, so there is no shared helper to reuse and its look has to be styled to match `web_src/css/modules/modal.css` by hand.

### Decision 2: where the dialog's markup and text come from
**Decision:** Render the empty `<dialog>` once in the base page template (next to the footer script) with its translated title, close label and "General" heading as server-rendered text, hidden until opened. JavaScript fills in the rows from `getShortcuts()` when `?` is pressed.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Build the whole dialog in JavaScript, and add its strings to `window.config.i18n` in `templates/base/head_script.tmpl`.
- (b) A Vue component mounted on demand, with its strings passed as `data-locale-*` attributes.

**Rationale:** The #56 registry already takes its descriptions and section labels as text the server translated into the page, so a server-rendered shell follows the same pattern. (a) would work, since `templates/base/head_script.tmpl` allows general texts in `window.config.i18n`, but it would split the dialog's text between two mechanisms and build markup in JavaScript that the template can hold. Vue (b) adds a component and a mount for a static list, which `.claude-students/docs/frontend-vue-components.md` advises against for markup this simple.

**Consequences:** Every page carries a few hundred bytes of hidden markup. Unlike `s` and `t`, which register from a `<kbd>` hint, `?` has no hint on the page, so it is registered from JavaScript with its description and "General" label read from the dialog's data attributes.

## Scope
medium (5 points)
> Sub-issue of #23 · estimate **2 points** (small) · blocked by #56 (unmerged); AC7's dialog listing needs #57

## User Story
As a user replying on an issue or pull request, I want GitHub's `r` shortcut to quote the text I have selected into my reply, or take me straight to the reply box when nothing is selected, so that I can answer a specific point without scrolling to the bottom or opening the comment's menu.

## User Scenario
A maintainer is reading a long issue thread. They select a sentence in someone's comment and press `r`. The page scrolls to the reply box at the bottom, the sentence is already in it as a Markdown quote, and the cursor sits after it, ready to type. Later, back at the top of the thread with nothing selected, they press `r` again and land in the same reply box with their text still there.

On a page with no reply box, such as an archived repository or when signed out, `r` does nothing.

| When the user presses `r` with | `r` does |
| --- | --- |
| Text selected inside one comment or the description | Quotes it into the reply box and puts the cursor after it |
| Nothing selected, or a selection that is not inside a single comment | Jumps to the reply box |
| No reply box on the page | Nothing |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given text is selected inside one comment or the issue description on an issue or pull request page, when the user presses `r`, then the text is added to the reply box as a Markdown quote (each line starting with `> `), the box scrolls into view, and the cursor is placed after the quote.
- [ ] AC2: Given the reply box already has text in it, when the user quotes with `r`, then the existing text is kept and the quote is added after it, separated by a blank line.
- [ ] AC3: Given nothing is selected, or the selection spans more than one comment or lies outside any comment, when the user presses `r`, then the reply box scrolls into view with the cursor at the end of its text, and the text is unchanged.
- [ ] AC4: Given the reply box is showing its Preview tab, when the user presses `r`, then it switches back to Write so the cursor and any quote can be seen.
- [ ] AC5: Given a page with no reply box (an archived repository, a signed-out visitor, or a locked conversation the user cannot comment on), when the user presses `r`, then nothing happens and no error is shown.
- [ ] AC6: Given focus is in the reply box or any other text field, when the user types `r`, then a literal `r` is typed.
- [ ] AC7: Given a page where `r` works, when the shortcuts are listed (`getShortcuts()`, shown by #57's dialog), then `r` has the description from the existing locale key `repo.issues.context.quote_reply` and a translated section label for issue and pull request pages.
- [ ] AC8: Unit tests cover the selection check in AC1 and AC3; a Playwright test in `tests/e2e/` covers AC1 and AC5 and calls `assertNoJsError`.

## Out of Scope
- Comments in code-review threads and their own reply boxes.
- GitHub's other issue page shortcuts (`a`, `l`, `m`, `q` and `x`).
- GitHub's `c` shortcuts: #59.
- Escape to leave the reply box; Tab already leaves it.
- Submitting the comment. `Ctrl`/`Cmd`+Enter already does that and is not touched here.
- Changes to what the "Quote reply" item in each comment's menu does.
- Showing the shortcuts to the user: #57.

## Open Questions
- None.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: how `r` puts the quote into the reply box
**Decision:** Pull the shared part of the existing "Quote reply" handler (`tryOnQuoteReply` in `web_src/js/features/repo-issue-edit.ts`) into a helper that takes a comment's content element and the reply editor, and appends the quoted selection, focuses the editor and moves the cursor to the end. The menu item and `r` both call it.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Have `r` find the comment the selection is in and click that comment's "Quote reply" menu item from code.
- (b) Write a separate handler for `r` that copies the selection-to-Markdown and append logic.

**Rationale:** (a) needs no refactor, but it ties `r` to the comment menu's markup and its click handler's `data-target` lookup. A change to the menu (for example the `<aria-menu>` migration work under #25) would break `r` without touching its code. (b) leaves two copies of the same quoting rules, so a fix to one (for example the lossy HTML-to-Markdown conversion noted in that file) would miss the other. A shared helper keeps one quoting rule, and the menu item keeps its current behaviour.

**Consequences:** The change touches the existing quote-reply code, so its behaviour needs checking by hand or by test as part of this issue. The helper also gains the switch back to the Write tab (AC4), which the menu item lacks today, so the menu item gets that fix too.

### Decision 2: when `r` is registered
**Decision:** Register `r` only when the page has a reply editor (`#comment-form .combo-markdown-editor`), passing that editor as the shortcut's `element` in #56's `registerShortcut`. Its translated description and section label come from `data-*` attributes the template puts on `#comment-form`.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Register `r` on every issue and pull request page, and have its action return early when there is no reply box.
- (b) Register it from a `<kbd>` hint in the template, the way #56 registers `s` and `t`.

**Rationale:** The server already decides whether to render the reply form (signed in, not archived, allowed to comment on a locked conversation), so registering from its presence gives AC5 with no permission logic in JavaScript. (a) would list `r` in #57's dialog on pages where it does nothing. (b) adds a visible hint to the reply box that GitHub does not show and the design does not call for.

**Consequences:** `r` and its dialog row exist only where they work. If the reply form is ever rendered on a page where the user cannot actually post, `r` follows the form, not the permission.

## Scope
small (2 points)

## User Story
As a keyboard user who suspects Gitea has shortcuts but cannot find them, I want to press `?` on any page and see the shortcuts that work on that page, grouped by section, so that I can learn them without reading the source or the docs.

## User Scenario
A user is on a repository's home page and presses `?`. A dialog titled "Keyboard shortcuts" opens in the middle of the page. It lists `?` under "General". It lists `S` ("Search code…") and `T` ("Go to file") under "Repository". Each row shows the keys as `<kbd>` elements next to the description. On the notifications page, no shortcuts belong to the page itself. There, `?` opens the same dialog and lists only `?`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given any page that loads Gitea's main script, and focus outside a text field, when the user presses `?`, then a dialog titled "Keyboard shortcuts" opens. It has one row for each shortcut that #56's `getShortcuts()` returns on that page, with the shortcut's keys and description.

- [ ] AC4: Given focus is in an input, a textarea or an editable area, when the user types `?`, then a `?` character appears in the field and the dialog does not open.
- [ ] AC5: Given shortcuts with different section labels, when the dialog opens, then each section is a heading with its shortcuts under it. A shortcut that later code registers with a new section appears under that section, with no change to the dialog's code.
- [ ] AC6: Given a page in a language other than English, when the dialog opens, then the title, the close button's accessible name and the "General" heading come from locale keys.
- [ ] AC7: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses `?` again, then the dialog stays open and unchanged, and no error occurs.
- [ ] AC8: Given the dialog is open, when the user presses the key of another shortcut on the page, then that shortcut does not run. For example, `s` on a repository home page does not move focus to the code search box.
- [ ] AC9: A Playwright test in `tests/e2e/` covers AC1, AC2, AC4 and AC8 on a repository home page and calls `assertNoJsError`. Unit tests in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` cover the grouping in AC5.

## Out of Scope
- Shortcuts other than `?`. The `g` shortcuts are #58, `c` is #59, and `r` is #95. Each one appears in the dialog when its issue registers it.
- Shortcuts that belong to other pages. The dialog lists only what works on the current page.
- Editing or remapping a shortcut from the dialog.
- The setting that turns shortcuts off. #60 adds that setting to this dialog as a checkbox.
- A link to the dialog in the footer or in a menu.
- A printable list or a documentation page of shortcuts.

## Open Questions
- Should the user also be able to open the dialog with the mouse, for example from a footer link? Proposed: not in this issue. One way in keeps the e2e test complete.
- Should a click on the backdrop close the dialog? Proposed: no. Escape and the close button are then the only ways out. Reviewer to confirm.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: build the dialog on the native `<dialog>` element
**Decision:** Build the dialog on the native `<dialog>` element and open it with `showModal()`.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) A Fomantic modal that `showFomanticModal` in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/modal.ts` opens. Gitea's other modals use this today.
- (b) A plain `<div>` with a focus trap, a backdrop and an Escape handler written by hand.

**Rationale:** `.claude-students/docs/frontend-js.md` says Fomantic is deprecated and that new features must not use it. Sibling issue #25 exists to remove Fomantic from the accessibility path, so a new Fomantic modal in an accessibility feature works against #25. `showModal()` makes the page behind the dialog inert (AC3), closes the dialog on Escape (AC2) and sets `aria-modal`. Option (b) would rewrite behaviour that the browser already has, and hand-written focus handling causes the kind of bug that #25 fixes.

**Consequences:** The browser provides most of AC2 and AC3, and the dialog needs no jQuery. Browsers differ on where focus goes when a dialog closes, so the close handler restores focus itself. #56's registry listens to key presses on the whole document, so the dialog must stop other shortcuts while it is open (AC8). This is the first native `<dialog>` in Gitea. No shared helper exists, and the dialog needs its own CSS to match `web_src/css/modules/modal.css`.

### Decision 2: render the dialog's markup and text on the server
**Decision:** Render the empty `<dialog>` once in the base page template, next to the footer script, and keep it hidden until it opens. The server renders the translated title, close label and "General" heading. When the user presses `?`, JavaScript adds the rows from `getShortcuts()`.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Build the whole dialog in JavaScript, and add its strings to `window.config.i18n` in `templates/base/head_script.tmpl`.
- (b) A Vue component that mounts on demand and receives its strings as `data-locale-*` attributes.

**Rationale:** The #56 registry already receives its descriptions and section labels as text that the server translated into the page. A dialog that the server renders follows the same pattern. Option (a) is possible, because `templates/base/head_script.tmpl` allows general texts in `window.config.i18n`. But (a) splits the dialog's text between two mechanisms, and it builds markup in JavaScript that the template can hold. Option (b) adds a component and a mount for a static list. `.claude-students/docs/frontend-vue-components.md` advises against Vue for markup this simple.

**Consequences:** Every page carries a few hundred bytes of hidden markup. The `s` and `t` shortcuts register from a `<kbd>` hint on the page, but `?` has no hint. JavaScript registers `?` instead, and reads its description and "General" label from data attributes on the dialog.

> Sub-issue of #23 · **P3** · estimate **2 points** (small) · blocked by #56 (unmerged) and #57; starts when #57's dialog exists

## User Story
As a user of speech recognition software, I want to turn off Gitea's single-character shortcuts, so that a word I dictate does not run a shortcut and move me away from what I was doing.

## User Scenario
A voice control user is on a repository page. Each time they dictate a word, focus jumps into the code search box. They press `?` and find a checkbox at the bottom of the shortcut dialog labelled "Enable character key shortcuts". They clear it, and the listed shortcuts turn grey. They close the dialog and dictate without interruption. The next time they open Gitea in that browser, shortcuts are still off.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given the user has cleared the "Enable character key shortcuts" checkbox in #57's dialog, when they press a registered shortcut other than `?`, then no shortcut runs. Focus stays where it was, and the key press is not default-prevented. For example, `s` on a repository home page does nothing.
- [ ] AC2: Given shortcuts are off, when the user reloads the page or opens another page in the same browser, then shortcuts are still off.
- [ ] AC3: Given shortcuts are off, when the user presses `?`, then the dialog still opens. The user can turn shortcuts back on without a mouse.
- [ ] AC4: Given shortcuts are off, when the user checks the box again, then `s` on a repository home page focuses the code search box again without a reload.
- [ ] AC5: Given a browser where storage access throws an error, when a page loads, then shortcuts are on, the checkbox is checked, and no uncaught error occurs.
- [ ] AC6: Given shortcuts are off, when the user presses `g` and then another key, then the registry does not hold `g` as the start of a sequence, and neither key runs a shortcut.
- [ ] AC7: Given a page in a language other than English, when the dialog opens, then the checkbox label comes from a locale key.
- [ ] AC8: Unit tests in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` cover AC1, AC3, AC5 and AC6. The e2e test from #57 gains a check for AC2.

## Out of Scope
- Remapping shortcuts, or turning off one shortcut at a time.
- Storing the setting on the server, or syncing it across browsers.
- A copy of the setting on the user settings pages.
- Keys that widgets own, such as the code editor's keys and the type-to-jump keys in menus. #56 already leaves these keys alone.

## Open Questions
- WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.4 accepts three options: turn off, remap, or active only on focus. This issue picks "turn off" as the smallest complete option. Reviewer to confirm this reading.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: store the setting in the browser
**Decision:** Store the setting with the existing `localUserSettings` wrapper in `web_src/js/modules/user-settings.ts`, under the key `keyboard-shortcuts-enabled`, with a default of `true`. Before it runs a shortcut, `handleKeyDown` in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts` reads the setting. `handleKeyDown` is the registry's only dispatch point.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) A per-user server setting in the existing `user_setting` key-value table (`models/user/setting.go`), with a checkbox on the Appearance settings page.
- (b) A cookie that the server reads, so that the server leaves the shortcut hints out of the page when shortcuts are off.

**Rationale:** Shortcuts also work for signed-out visitors, and option (a) has nowhere to store a signed-out visitor's choice. The preference also belongs to one machine. Someone who uses voice control on one machine does not need shortcuts off on every machine. Option (b) lets the server skip the hints, but the browser then sends the cookie with every request, and a behaviour that lives in the browser needs a server change. `localUserSettings` already wraps every storage call in try/catch, so AC5 needs no new error handling.

**Consequences:** The server does not change. The setting does not follow the user to another browser, and support staff cannot see it.

### Decision 2: keep `?` working when shortcuts are off
**Decision:** The setting turns off every character shortcut except `?`.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Turn off every shortcut, `?` included. This is the most literal reading of SC 2.1.4.
- (b) Use SC 2.1.4's "active only on focus" option, so that shortcuts run only while one component has focus.

**Rationale:** With option (a), a keyboard-only user who turns shortcuts off has no keyboard path back to the checkbox. Option (a) swaps one accessibility failure for another. One exempt key is the usual way back. Option (b) suits a widget's own keys, but Gitea's shortcuts act on the whole page. For example, `s` moves focus to the code search box from anywhere on the page. If shortcuts worked only inside one component, they would lose their purpose.

**Consequences:** `?` stays active as a deliberate exception. The check carries a short code comment that says why, so that nobody removes the exception later. A user who dictates "?" still opens the dialog. The dialog does no harm and closes with Escape.

> Sub-issue of #23 · estimate **2 points** (small) · blocked by #56 (unmerged); AC7's dialog listing needs #57

## User Story
As a user who replies on an issue or a pull request, I want GitHub's `r` shortcut to quote my selected text into my reply, or to take me to the reply box when nothing is selected, so that I can answer a specific point without scrolling to the bottom or opening the comment's menu.

## User Scenario
A maintainer reads a long issue thread. They select a sentence in someone's comment and press `r`. The page scrolls to the reply box at the bottom. The sentence is already in the box as a Markdown quote, and the cursor is after it, ready for typing. Later, the maintainer is back at the top of the thread with nothing selected. They press `r` again and land in the same reply box, with their text still there.

On a page with no reply box, `r` does nothing. Archived repositories and signed-out visitors are two examples.

| When the user presses `r` with | `r` does |
| --- | --- |
| Text selected inside one comment or the description | Quotes the text into the reply box and puts the cursor after it |
| Nothing selected, or a selection that is not inside one comment | Moves to the reply box |
| No reply box on the page | Nothing |

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given text is selected inside one comment or inside the issue description, on an issue or pull request page, when the user presses `r`, then the reply box gets the text as a Markdown quote, with `> ` at the start of each line. The box scrolls into view, and the cursor is after the quote.
- [ ] AC2: Given the reply box already has text, when the user quotes with `r`, then the existing text stays, and the quote follows it after a blank line.
- [ ] AC3: Given nothing is selected, or the selection spans more than one comment, or the selection is outside every comment, when the user presses `r`, then the reply box scrolls into view. The cursor is at the end of the box's text, and the text does not change.
- [ ] AC4: Given the reply box shows its Preview tab, when the user presses `r`, then the box switches back to the Write tab, so the cursor and any quote are visible.
- [ ] AC5: Given a page with no reply box, when the user presses `r`, then nothing happens and no error appears. Pages with no reply box include an archived repository, any page for a signed-out visitor, and a locked conversation that the user cannot comment on.
- [ ] AC6: Given focus is in the reply box or in any other text field, when the user types `r`, then an `r` character appears in the field.
- [ ] AC7: Given a page where `r` works, when the shortcuts are listed by `getShortcuts()` or #57's dialog, then `r` has the description from the existing locale key `repo.issues.context.quote_reply`, and a translated section label for issue and pull request pages.
- [ ] AC8: Unit tests cover the selection check in AC1 and AC3. A Playwright test in `tests/e2e/` covers AC1 and AC5 and calls `assertNoJsError`.

## Out of Scope
- Comments in code review threads, and the reply boxes of those threads.
- GitHub's other issue page shortcuts: `a`, `l`, `m`, `q` and `x`.
- GitHub's `c` shortcuts. #59 adds them.
- Escape to leave the reply box. Tab already leaves it.
- Submitting the comment. `Ctrl+Enter` and `Cmd+Enter` already submit it, and this issue does not change them.
- Changes to what the "Quote reply" item in each comment's menu does.
- Showing the shortcuts to the user. #57 adds the dialog that does this.

## Open Questions
- None.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: share one quoting helper with the "Quote reply" menu item
**Decision:** Move the shared part of the existing "Quote reply" handler, `tryOnQuoteReply` in `web_src/js/features/repo-issue-edit.ts`, into a helper. The helper takes a comment's content element and the reply editor. It appends the quoted selection, focuses the editor, and moves the cursor to the end. The menu item and `r` both call the helper.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) `r` finds the comment that holds the selection, and clicks that comment's "Quote reply" menu item from code.
- (b) A separate handler for `r` with its own copy of the code that converts the selection to Markdown and appends it.

**Rationale:** Option (a) needs no refactor, but it ties `r` to the comment menu's markup and to the `data-target` lookup in the menu's click handler. A change to the menu, such as the `<aria-menu>` migration work under #25, would break `r` without any change to the code for `r`. Option (b) keeps two copies of the quoting code. A fix to one copy would miss the other. One example is the lossy HTML-to-Markdown conversion that a comment in `repo-issue-edit.ts` notes. With a shared helper, there is one copy of the quoting code, and the menu item keeps its current behaviour.

**Consequences:** The change touches the existing quote-reply code, so this issue must check that code's behaviour, by hand or with a test. The helper also switches the reply box back to the Write tab (AC4). The menu item does not do this today, so the menu item gets the same fix.

### Decision 2: register `r` only on pages with a reply box
**Decision:** Register `r` only when the page has a reply editor (`#comment-form .combo-markdown-editor`), and pass that editor as the shortcut's `element` to #56's `registerShortcut`. The template puts `data-*` attributes on `#comment-form` that hold the translated description and section label of `r`.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Register `r` on every issue and pull request page, and make its action return early when the page has no reply box.
- (b) Register `r` from a `<kbd>` hint in the template, the way #56 registers `s` and `t`.

**Rationale:** The server already decides whether to render the reply form. It checks that the user is signed in, that the repository is not archived, and that the user may comment on a locked conversation. Registration that depends on the form gives AC5, with no permission logic in JavaScript. With option (a), #57's dialog lists `r` on pages where `r` does nothing. Option (b) adds a visible hint to the reply box. GitHub shows no such hint, and this design does not need one.

**Consequences:** `r` and its row in the dialog exist only on pages where `r` works. If a future template renders the reply form on a page where the user cannot post, `r` still registers there. Registration follows the form, not the user's permission.

> Sub-issue of #25 · **P1** · estimate **2 points** (small) · blocked by nothing

## User Story
As a contributor who changes dropdown code, I want end-to-end tests that fail when a dropdown's ARIA state no longer matches what a keyboard user sees, so that a later refactor cannot undo the Sprint 1 accessibility work without anyone noticing.

## User Scenario
A contributor opens a PR that changes `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts`. CI runs the label picker test on an issue page. The test opens the picker from the keyboard and checks that `aria-expanded` changes to `true`. It presses ArrowDown and checks that `aria-activedescendant` names one of the picker's options. It presses Escape and checks that the list closed. The contributor's change removed `aria-controls`, so the test fails, and the failure names that assertion.

A second contributor changes `<aria-menu>` and removes `aria-haspopup` from the navbar avatar menu. The navbar test fails and names the missing attribute.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given a signed-in user on an issue with seeded labels, when the test opens the sidebar label picker from the keyboard, then the test asserts three things about the picker's focusable element. Its role is `combobox`. Its `aria-expanded` is `false` before the picker opens and `true` after. Its `aria-controls` names the picker's list.
- [ ] AC2: Given the label picker is open, when the test presses ArrowDown, then the test asserts that `aria-activedescendant` names an existing element with role `option` inside the picker's list.
- [ ] AC3: Given the label picker is open, when the test presses Escape, then the test asserts that the list is hidden, that focus is still on the picker, and that `aria-expanded` is `false`.
- [ ] AC4: Given the signed-in navbar, then `tests/e2e/menus.test.ts` asserts that each `<aria-menu>` trigger has `aria-haspopup="menu"`, and that the trigger's `aria-controls` names an element with role `menu`.
- [ ] AC5: Each new or extended test calls `assertNoJsError` from `tests/e2e/utils.ts` and finishes in less than 2 seconds on a local machine.
- [ ] AC6: The tests run with `GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='<the test file>' make test-e2e`. Every assertion passes on `main`, with one exception. An assertion that finds a bug gets a `test.fail` marker and a link to a new issue for that bug. Out of Scope describes this rule.

## Out of Scope
- Fixing what the tests find. Each failing assertion gets a new bug issue and a `test.fail` marker that links to the issue. The suite then records the bug, and the marked test starts to fail when someone fixes the bug. This issue does not change product code.
- Navbar keyboard behaviour that `tests/e2e/menus.test.ts` and `tests/e2e/aria-menu.test.ts` already cover: opening, arrow keys, Home and End, Escape, and type-to-jump.
- The `aria-selected` checks and label announcement checks that `tests/e2e/multiselect-aria.test.ts` already has.
- Adding `axe-core` or any other accessibility-testing dependency.
- Tests for every Fomantic dropdown.
- Screen reader output. No automated test can check it.

## Open Questions
- `dropdown.ts` updates `aria-expanded` on focus, blur, mouseup and arrow-key keyup. It does not appear to update it on Escape, so the last check in AC3 may fail on `main`. This is from reading the code. Nobody has run the check yet. The implementation runs that check first. If the check fails, the implementer files a bug as AC6 describes.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: assert ARIA state in Playwright
**Decision:** Assert the ARIA attributes and the focus position directly in Playwright.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Add `@axe-core/playwright` and assert that the page has no violations.
- (b) Add the checks to the vitest unit tests in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.test.ts`. Those tests already start real Fomantic dropdowns in happy-dom.

**Rationale:** Option (a) adds a dependency, and axe reports on the page's markup in general, not on the state that a keyboard user depends on. Axe would not catch an `aria-activedescendant` that points at the wrong option. An axe failure in another part of the page would also fail the test for an unrelated reason. Option (b) can check static attributes. But the bugs that this suite guards against happen during real key sequences. `dropdown.ts` updates the ARIA state on a timer after keyup, and Fomantic animates the list when it opens and closes. Unit tests would have to fake the same timing they are meant to check.

**Consequences:** A failing assertion names the exact attribute that broke. The assertions depend on the current Fomantic markup. If work under #25 moves the label picker off Fomantic, this test needs updates, and a comment in the test says so.

### Decision 2: extend the label picker test and the navbar test
**Decision:** Add the `aria-expanded`, `aria-activedescendant` and `aria-controls` checks for the issue label picker to `tests/e2e/multiselect-aria.test.ts`. Add the `aria-haspopup` and `aria-controls` checks to the existing navbar test.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) A full keyboard suite for the navbar avatar menu, as the first draft of this issue planned.
- (b) A new test for the repository template search on `/repo/create`.

**Rationale:** Since #62 merged, the navbar menus are `<aria-menu>` elements, and `tests/e2e/menus.test.ts` already drives the avatar menu from the keyboard. Option (a) would mostly repeat that test. Option (b) also tests a combobox, but its options load from the API after the list opens. The test then needs waits, which make it slower and less stable. The label picker has the same combobox role. The test seeds its labels, and `multiselect-aria.test.ts` already opens the picker. The new checks add a few lines to an existing test.

**Consequences:** The suite stays under the 2-second target and needs no new test file. Search dropdowns that load their options from the API, such as the template search, still have no end-to-end test.

---
name: shortcut-registry-56
description: "#56 (ab-wm's keyboard-shortcut registry) blocks the user's #57, #60 and #95; branch, API as of 2026-10-18, and how to build on it."
metadata:
  type: project
---

#56 is ab-wm's central keyboard-shortcut registry. The user's #57 (`?` dialog), #60 (turn shortcuts off) and #95 (`r` quote reply) all build on it. #65 does not, so it can start first. See [[sprint2-deliverables]].

**State on 2026-10-18:** the code was on branch `origin/refactor/issue-56-impl`, with the last commit on 10-18. It had no PR and was not merged. ab-wm's spec reviews on all four issues said to "pay attention to the changes introduced by #56".

**API on that branch** (`web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts`):
- `registerShortcut({keys, description, section?, element?, action})` registers a shortcut. `keys` is a space-separated sequence, such as `"g c"`. `description` and `section` arrive already translated from the server, through data attributes or a placeholder. A shortcut with an `element` lives only while that element is connected. Exact or prefix clashes throw.
- `getShortcuts()` returns the list that #57's dialog reads.
- `handleKeyDown` is the only dispatch point, where #60's off switch goes. It skips inputs, textareas, selects and contenteditable, modifier keys, and events another handler already prevented.
- `initShortcutKbd` registers `s` and `t` from `<kbd>` hints, under the section "Repository". Nothing registers `?` yet.
- Unit tests are in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts`.

**Why:** ab-wm owns #56, and the API can change before it merges. The specs for #57, #60 and #95 name these functions, so a rename means updating those issue bodies too.

**How to apply:** before implementing #57, #60 or #95, check the state live. Use `gh pr list --search 56` and `git log origin/refactor/issue-56-impl`, and re-read `shortcut.ts`. Branch from `main` only after #56 merges; never merge ab-wm's branch into the user's own branch (COURSE-WORKFLOW). If #56 is late, raise it with ab-wm early, because a sprint with no merged PR scores 0.
